```
1→-- Add RLS policies to users table to prevent security vulnerabilities
     2→-- This fixes the critical issue where users could read other users' data and modify their own credits
     3→
     4→-- Enable RLS on users table
     5→ALTER TABLE users ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
     6→
     7→-- Policy: Users can only read their own user record
     8→CREATE POLICY "Users can view their own record"
     9→  ON users
    10→  FOR SELECT
    11→  USING (auth.uid() = id);
    12→
    13→-- Policy: Users can only update their own name, email, api_keys, and settings
    14→CREATE POLICY "Users can update their own profile"
    15→  ON users
    16→  FOR UPDATE
    17→  USING (auth.uid() = id);
    18→
    19→-- Policy: Only service role can insert new users
    20→CREATE POLICY "Service role can insert users"
    21→  ON users
    22→  FOR INSERT
    23→  WITH CHECK (auth.role() = 'service_role');
    24→
    25→-- Policy: Only service role can delete users
    26→CREATE POLICY "Service role can delete users"
    27→  ON users
    28→  FOR DELETE
    29→  USING (auth.role() = 'service_role');
    30→
    31→-- Policy: Service role can do everything (overrides other policies)
    32→CREATE POLICY "Service role can do everything on users"
    33→  ON users
    34→  FOR ALL
    35→  TO service_role
    36→  USING (true)
    37→  WITH CHECK (true);
```

```
    64→-- Policy: Users can view shots that belong to their projects
    65→CREATE POLICY "Users can view their own shots" ON shots
    66→  FOR SELECT
    67→  USING (
    68→    project_id IN (SELECT id FROM projects WHERE user_id = auth.uid())
    69→  );
    70→
    71→-- Policy: Users can insert shots into their own projects
    72→CREATE POLICY "Users can insert their own shots" ON shots
    73→  FOR INSERT
    74→  WITH CHECK (
    75→    project_id IN (SELECT id FROM projects WHERE user_id = auth.uid())
    76→  );
    77→
    78→-- Policy: Users can update shots in their own projects
    79→CREATE POLICY "Users can update their own shots" ON shots
    80→  FOR UPDATE
    81→  USING (
    82→    project_id IN (SELECT id FROM projects WHERE user_id = auth.uid())
    83→  );
    84→
    85→-- Policy: Users can delete shots from their own projects
    86→CREATE POLICY "Users can delete their own shots" ON shots
    87→  FOR DELETE
    88→  USING (
    89→    project_id IN (SELECT id FROM projects WHERE user_id = auth.uid())
    90→  );
    91→
    92→-- Policy: Service role can manage all shots
    93→CREATE POLICY "Service role can manage all shots" ON shots
    94→  FOR ALL
    95→  TO service_role
    96→  USING (true)
    97→  WITH CHECK (true);
    98→
    99→-- ============================================================================
   100→-- 3. FIX shot_generations POLICY - The existing policy is broken (no user check)
   101→-- ============================================================================
   102→
   103→-- Drop the broken policy
   104→DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Users can manage their shot generations" ON shot_generations;
   105→
   106→-- Create proper policy that checks ownership through shot -> project -> user
   107→CREATE POLICY "Users can manage their shot generations" ON shot_generations
   108→  FOR ALL
   109→  USING (
   110→    EXISTS (
   111→      SELECT 1 FROM shots s
   112→      JOIN projects p ON s.project_id = p.id
   113→      WHERE s.id = shot_generations.shot_id
   114→      AND p.user_id = auth.uid()
   115→    )
   116→  )
   117→  WITH CHECK (
   118→    EXISTS (
   119→      SELECT 1 FROM shots s
   120→      JOIN projects p ON s.project_id = p.id
   121→      WHERE s.id = shot_generations.shot_id
   122→      AND p.user_id = auth.uid()
   123→    )
   124→  );
   125→
   126→-- Policy: Service role can manage all shot_generations
   127→DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Service role can manage all shot_generations" ON shot_generations;
   128→CREATE POLICY "Service role can manage all shot_generations" ON shot_generations
   129→  FOR ALL
   130→  TO service_role
   131→  USING (true)
   132→  WITH CHECK (true);
   133→
   134→-- ============================================================================
   135→-- 4. COMMENTS
   136→-- ============================================================================
   137→
   138→COMMENT ON POLICY "Users can view their own projects" ON projects IS 
   139→  'Critical security fix: Users can only access their own projects. Prevents cross-user data leakage.';
   140→
   141→COMMENT ON POLICY "Users can view their own shots" ON shots IS 
   142→  'Critical security fix: Users can only access shots within their projects.';
   143→
   144→COMMENT ON POLICY "Users can manage their shot generations" ON shot_generations IS 
   145→  'Fixes broken policy: Now properly checks user ownership through shot -> project -> user chain.';
   146→
   147→-- ============================================================================
   148→-- 5. VERIFICATION
   149→-- ============================================================================
   150→
   151→DO $$
   152→DECLARE
   153→  projects_rls boolean;
   154→  shots_rls boolean;
   155→  shot_gens_rls boolean;
   156→BEGIN
   157→  -- Check RLS is enabled
   158→  SELECT relrowsecurity INTO projects_rls FROM pg_class WHERE relname = 'projects';
   159→  SELECT relrowsecurity INTO shots_rls FROM pg_class WHERE relname = 'shots';
   160→  SELECT relrowsecurity INTO shot_gens_rls FROM pg_class WHERE relname = 'shot_generations';
   161→  
   162→  IF NOT projects_rls THEN
   163→    RAISE EXCEPTION 'CRITICAL: RLS not enabled on projects table';
   164→  END IF;
   165→  
   166→  IF NOT shots_rls THEN
   167→    RAISE EXCEPTION 'CRITICAL: RLS not enabled on shots table';
   168→  END IF;
   169→  
   170→  IF NOT shot_gens_rls THEN
   171→    RAISE EXCEPTION 'CRITICAL: RLS not enabled on shot_generations table';
   172→  END IF;
   173→  
   174→  RAISE NOTICE '✅ SECURITY FIX APPLIED: RLS enabled on projects, shots, and shot_generations';
   175→  RAISE NOTICE '✅ All ownership policies created successfully';
   176→END $$;
   177→
   178→
   179→
   180→
   181→
   182→
   183→
```

## Security Issues Analysis

I've thoroughly investigated both security issues. Here's the detailed breakdown:

## **ISSUE #1: SECURITY DEFINER Settings RPC - Missing Ownership Check**

### Location
- **File**: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/migrations/20250116000001_fix_atomic_update_found_check.sql`
- **Function**: `update_tool_settings_atomic(p_table_name, p_id, p_tool_id, p_settings)`
- **Language**: PL/pgSQL with `SECURITY DEFINER`

### The Vulnerability
The RPC is marked `SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public`, which means:
1. **Browser-callable**: It's callable directly from the browser via `rpc()` in TypeScript (confirmed in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/integrations/supabase/repositories/toolSettingsWriteRepository.ts` line 34)
2. **Runs as superuser**: The function executes with elevated database permissions
3. **No ownership verification**: The function accepts `p_table_name`, `p_id`, and updates ANY row in those tables WITHOUT checking if the caller owns it

### Current Code
```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION update_tool_settings_atomic(
  p_table_name text,
  p_id uuid,
  p_tool_id text,
  p_settings jsonb
)
RETURNS void
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_rows_affected integer;
BEGIN
  IF p_table_name NOT IN ('users', 'projects', 'shots') THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Invalid table name: %', p_table_name;
  END IF;
  
  EXECUTE format(
    'UPDATE %I SET settings = jsonb_set(COALESCE(settings, ''{}''::jsonb), ARRAY[%L], %L::jsonb, true) WHERE id = %L',
    p_table_name, p_tool_id, p_settings, p_id
  );
  
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows_affected = ROW_COUNT;
  
  IF v_rows_affected = 0 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'No % found with id %', p_table_name, p_id;
  END IF;
END;
$$;
```

### Why This Is a Problem
- **User A** can call `rpc('update_tool_settings_atomic', { p_table_name: 'users', p_id: '<User B UUID>', p_tool_id: 'travel', p_settings: {...} })`
- **User A** can update **User B's** settings because there's no ownership check
- **User A** can update settings in any **project** or **shot** they don't own
- The function ignores RLS policies (runs as superuser with `SECURITY DEFINER`)

### The Fix
**Add ownership verification BEFORE the UPDATE statement:**

```sql
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION update_tool_settings_atomic(
  p_table_name text,
  p_id uuid,
  p_tool_id text,
  p_settings jsonb
)
RETURNS void
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = public
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_rows_affected integer;
  v_current_user_id uuid := auth.uid();
BEGIN
  IF p_table_name NOT IN ('users', 'projects', 'shots') THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Invalid table name: %', p_table_name;
  END IF;

  -- CRITICAL: Ownership check based on table type
  IF p_table_name = 'users' THEN
    -- Users can only update their own record
    IF p_id != v_current_user_id THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'Forbidden: Cannot update other users'' settings';
    END IF;
  ELSIF p_table_name = 'projects' THEN
    -- Users can only update projects they own
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM projects WHERE id = p_id AND user_id = v_current_user_id) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'Forbidden: Cannot update projects you do not own';
    END IF;
  ELSIF p_table_name = 'shots' THEN
    -- Users can only update shots in their own projects
    IF NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM shots s
      JOIN projects p ON s.project_id = p.id
      WHERE s.id = p_id AND p.user_id = v_current_user_id
    ) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'Forbidden: Cannot update shots in projects you do not own';
    END IF;
  END IF;
  
  EXECUTE format(
    'UPDATE %I SET settings = jsonb_set(COALESCE(settings, ''{}''::jsonb), ARRAY[%L], %L::jsonb, true) WHERE id = %L',
    p_table_name, p_tool_id, p_settings, p_id
  );
  
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows_affected = ROW_COUNT;
  
  IF v_rows_affected = 0 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'No % found with id %', p_table_name, p_id;
  END IF;
END;
$$;
```

### How to Verify It Works
1. **Test unauthorized access is blocked**:
   ```typescript
   // As User A, try to update User B's settings
   const { error } = await supabaseClient.rpc('update_tool_settings_atomic', {
     p_table_name: 'users',
     p_id: 'user-b-uuid',  // Another user's ID
     p_tool_id: 'travel',
     p_settings: { model: 'claude' }
   });
   // Should return: "Forbidden: Cannot update other users' settings"
   ```

2. **Test authorized access still works**:
   ```typescript
   // As User A, update own settings
   const { error } = await supabaseClient.rpc('update_tool_settings_atomic', {
     p_table_name: 'users',
     p_id: auth.uid(),  // Own ID
     p_tool_id: 'travel',
     p_settings: { model: 'claude' }
   });
   // Should succeed
   ```

3. **Test cross-project access is blocked**:
   ```typescript
   // As User A, try to update a shot in User B's project
   const { error } = await supabaseClient.rpc('update_tool_settings_atomic', {
     p_table_name: 'shots',
     p_id: 'shot-from-user-b-project',
     p_tool_id: 'travel',
     p_settings: {}
   });
   // Should return: "Forbidden: Cannot update shots in projects you do not own"
   ```

## **ISSUE #2: get-task-status Leaks Task Access Without Ownership Check**

### Location
- **File**: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/get-task-status/index.ts`
- **Function**: The `serve()` handler

### The Vulnerability
The function:
1. **Authenticates the request** (line 54): Checks for valid Bearer token
2. **DOES NOT verify task ownership** (lines 60-67): Directly queries the task by ID without checking if the caller owns it
3. **Returns the task status** to any authenticated user for any task

### Current Code (lines 54-73)
```typescript
const auth = await authenticateRequest(req, supabaseAdmin, "[GET-TASK-STATUS]");
if (!auth.success) {
  return new Response(auth.error || "Authentication failed", { status: auth.statusCode || 403 });
}

try {
  const { data: task, error } = await supabaseAdmin
    .from("tasks")
    .select("status")
    .eq("id", taskId)
    .single();

  if (error || !task) {
    return new Response("Task not found", { status: 404 });
  }

  return new Response(JSON.stringify({ status: task.status }), {
    status: 200,
    headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  });
```

### Why This Is a Problem
- **User A** can call `POST /functions/v1/get-task-status` with `{ task_id: <any-uuid> }`
- As long as **User A** is authenticated (has a valid PAT or JWT), they get the task status
- **User A** can enumerate ALL task IDs in the system and discover their status
- **User A** can monitor other users' generation progress without permission

### How get-task-output Does It Right
Contrast with `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/supabase/functions/get-task-output/index.ts` (lines 51-64):

```typescript
const actor = await authorizeTaskActor({
  supabaseAdmin,
  taskId,
  auth: auth!,
  logPrefix: "[GET-TASK-OUTPUT]",
});
if (!actor.ok) {
  logger.error("Task access denied", {
    task_id: taskId,
    error: actor.error,
    status_code: actor.statusCode,
  });
  return jsonResponse({ error: actor.error }, actor.statusCode);
}

// Fetch the task with all needed fields
const { data: task, error: taskError } = await supabaseAdmin
  .from("tasks")
  .select("id, status, output_location, project_id, params, dependant_on")
  .eq("id", taskId)
  .single();
```

**Key difference**: `authorizeTaskActor()` (from `taskActorPolicy.ts`) verifies:
- If caller is service role → allow (lines 35-44)
- If caller is a user → verify they own the task's project (lines 46-75)

### The Fix
**Add the same ownership check that get-task-output uses:**

```typescript
import { authorizeTaskActor } from "../_shared/taskActorPolicy.ts";

serve(async (req) => {
  const serviceKey = Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY");
  const supabaseUrl = Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_URL");

  if (!serviceKey || !supabaseUrl) {
    return new Response("Server configuration error", { status: 500 });
  }

  const supabaseAdmin = createClient(supabaseUrl, serviceKey);
  const logger = new SystemLogger(supabaseAdmin, 'get-task-status');

  if (req.method !== "POST") {
    return new Response("Method not allowed", { status: 405 });
  }

  let requestBody: unknown = {};
  try {
    const bodyText = await req.text();
    if (bodyText) {
      requestBody = JSON.parse(bodyText);
    }
  } catch {
    return new Response("Invalid JSON body", { status: 400 });
  }

  const taskId = requestBody.task_id;
  if (!taskId) {
    return new Response("task_id is required", { status: 400 });
  }

  const auth = await authenticateRequest(req, supabaseAdmin, "[GET-TASK-STATUS]");
  if (!auth.success) {
    return new Response(auth.error || "Authentication failed", { status: auth.statusCode || 403 });
  }

  // ADD THIS OWNERSHIP CHECK:
  const actor = await authorizeTaskActor({
    supabaseAdmin,
    taskId,
    auth,
    logPrefix: "[GET-TASK-STATUS]",
  });
  if (!actor.ok) {
    logger.error("Task access denied", {
      task_id: taskId,
      error: actor.error,
      status_code: actor.statusCode,
    });
    return new Response(
      JSON.stringify({ error: actor.error }),
      { status: actor.statusCode, headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } }
    );
  }

  try {
    const { data: task, error } = await supabaseAdmin
      .from("tasks")
      .select("status")
      .eq("id", taskId)
      .single();

    if (error || !task) {
      return new Response("Task not found", { status: 404 });
    }

    return new Response(JSON.stringify({ status: task.status }), {
      status: 200,
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    });
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    logger.error('Internal server error', { task_id: taskId, error: error?.message });
    await logger.flush();
    return new Response(`Internal server error: ${error?.message}`, { status: 500 });
  }
});
```

### How to Verify It Works
1. **Test unauthorized access is blocked**:
   ```bash
   # As User A with PAT, try to get status of task owned by User B
   curl -X POST http://localhost:54321/functions/v1/get-task-status \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer user-a-pat" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"task_id": "task-owned-by-user-b"}'
   # Should return: 403 Forbidden with "Forbidden" error
   ```

2. **Test authorized access still works**:
   ```bash
   # As User A with PAT, get status of own task
   curl -X POST http://localhost:54321/functions/v1/get-task-status \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer user-a-pat" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"task_id": "task-owned-by-user-a"}'
   # Should return: 200 OK with { status: "..." }
   ```

3. **Test service role still works**:
   ```bash
   # As service role, get status of any task
   curl -X POST http://localhost:54321/functions/v1/get-task-status \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"task_id": "any-task-id"}'
   # Should return: 200 OK with { status: "..." }
   ```

## Summary Table

| Issue | File | Problem | Fix | Impact |
|-------|------|---------|-----|--------|
| **RPC** | `20250116000001_fix_atomic_update_found_check.sql` | `update_tool_settings_atomic` runs as `SECURITY DEFINER` with no ownership checks | Add `auth.uid()` validation for users/projects/shots before UPDATE | User A can modify User B's settings |
| **Edge Fn** | `get-task-status/index.ts` | Returns task status to ANY authenticated user without verifying ownership | Call `authorizeTaskActor()` before querying task | User A can enumerate/monitor User B's tasks |

Both fixes follow the **same pattern**: verify the caller is service role OR owns the resource before proceeding.

## Analysis: Incomplete Structure Video Migration

### The Problem

The reigh codebase has **4 incomplete structure-video field migrations** (38.4% severity). The issue is a **dual-contract system** where the old single-video model coexists with the new multi-video model, causing:

1. **Internal UI layer duplication** - both `primaryStructureVideo*` (legacy) and `structureVideos` (canonical) fields throughout components and contexts
2. **Deprecated fields still in active emission** - segment task submission still builds `LegacyStructureVideoConfig` objects with deprecated field names
3. **Fallback chains** - multiple adapters converting between contracts, increasing complexity
4. **No clear ownership** - migration path unclear, no single source of truth

### Migration Timeline: Old → New Contract

**Old Contract (Single Video, Top-Level Fields):**
```
structure_video_path: string
structure_video_treatment: 'adjust' | 'clip'
structure_video_motion_strength: number
structure_video_type: 'uni3c' | 'flow' | 'canny' | 'depth'
uni3c_start_percent: number
uni3c_end_percent: number
use_uni3c: boolean
```

**New Contract (Multi-Video Array with Structure Guidance):**
```
structure_videos: [
  {
    path: string
    start_frame: number
    end_frame: number
    treatment?: 'adjust' | 'clip'
    source_start_frame?: number
    source_end_frame?: number
  }
]
structure_guidance: {
  target: 'vace' | 'uni3c'
  preprocessing?: 'flow' | 'canny' | 'depth' | 'none'
  strength?: number
  canny_intensity?: number
  depth_contrast?: number
  step_window?: [number, number]  // [start%, end%]
  frame_policy?: 'fit' | 'clip'
  zero_empty_frames?: boolean
}
```

### Key Files in Migration State

#### Type Definitions (Source of Truth)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages/types.ts` — **canonical** `StructureVideoConfig` and `StructureGuidanceConfig` defined here
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages/uiTypes.ts` — **editor-facing UI model** `StructureVideoConfigWithMetadata` (adds metadata + legacy UI fields)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/shared/lib/tasks/travelBetweenImages/legacyStructureVideo.ts` — **deprecation shim** with `LegacyStructureVideoConfig` and migration adapters

#### Internal Contract Duplication (Problematic)
1. **`src/tools/travel-between-images/components/ShotImagesEditor/types.ts`** (lines 76-87)
   - Declares BOTH `primaryStructureVideo*` fields (legacy) AND `structureVideos` (canonical)
   - Used by all child components of ShotImagesEditor

2. **`src/tools/travel-between-images/components/Timeline/TimelineMediaContext.tsx`** (lines 11-33)
   - Mirror duplication: legacy `primaryStructureVideo*` + `onPrimaryStructureVideoInputChange` 
   - Canonical `structureVideos` + add/update/remove callbacks
   - Comments explicitly say "use canonical" but both contracts actively used

3. **`src/tools/travel-between-images/components/Timeline/TimelineContainer/components/GuidanceVideoControls.tsx`**
   - Branches on which callback to use (new vs legacy)

#### Active Deprecated Field Emission

       ```python
     triage_ever_completed = bool(meta.get("last_completed_at"))
       ```

```
1→/**
     2→ * buildImageEditStateValue — shared factory for constructing ImageEditState.
     3→ *
     4→ * Both useImageEditOrchestrator (lightbox) and useInlineEditState (inline editor)
     5→ * build the same ~60-field ImageEditState from the same four hooks.
     6→ * This factory eliminates that duplication.
     7→ */
     8→
     9→import type { ImageEditState, ImageEditMode } from '../contexts/ImageEditContext';
    10→import type { EditAdvancedSettings, LoraMode, QwenEditModel } from './editSettingsTypes';
    11→import type { useInpainting } from '../hooks/useInpainting';
    12→import type { useMagicEditMode } from '../hooks/useMagicEditMode';
    13→import type { useRepositionMode } from '../hooks/useRepositionMode';
    14→import type { useImg2ImgMode } from '../hooks/useImg2ImgMode';
    15→
    16→interface BuildImageEditStateParams {
    17→  // Hook results (provide all canvas/status fields)
    18→  inpainting: ReturnType<typeof useInpainting>;
    19→  magic: ReturnType<typeof useMagicEditMode>;
    20→  reposition: ReturnType<typeof useRepositionMode>;
    21→  img2img: ReturnType<typeof useImg2ImgMode>;
    22→
    23→  // Display
    24→  imageContainerRef: React.RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null>;
    25→
    26→  // Overrides (where orchestrator and inline callers diverge)
    27→  handleExitInpaintMode: () => void;
    28→  setEditMode: (mode: ImageEditMode) => void;
    29→
    30→  // Settings (sourced from different places per caller)
    31→  loraMode: LoraMode;
    32→  setLoraMode: (mode: LoraMode) => void;
    33→  customLoraUrl: string;
    34→  setCustomLoraUrl: (url: string) => void;
    35→  createAsGeneration: boolean;
    36→  setCreateAsGeneration: (value: boolean) => void;
    37→  qwenEditModel: QwenEditModel;
    38→  setQwenEditModel: (model: QwenEditModel) => void;
    39→  advancedSettings: EditAdvancedSettings;
    40→  setAdvancedSettings: (updates: Partial<EditAdvancedSettings>) => void;
    41→}
    42→
    43→export function buildImageEditStateValue(p: BuildImageEditStateParams): ImageEditState {
    44→  const { inpainting, magic, reposition, img2img } = p;
    45→
    46→  return {
    47→    // Mode state
    48→    isInpaintMode: inpainting.isInpaintMode,
    49→    isMagicEditMode: magic.isMagicEditMode,
    50→    isSpecialEditMode: magic.isSpecialEditMode,
    51→    editMode: inpainting.editMode as ImageEditState['editMode'],
    52→
    53→    // Mode setters
    54→    setIsInpaintMode: inpainting.setIsInpaintMode,
    55→    setIsMagicEditMode: magic.setIsMagicEditMode,
    56→    setEditMode: p.setEditMode,
    57→
    58→    // Mode entry/exit
    59→    handleEnterInpaintMode: inpainting.handleEnterInpaintMode,
    60→    handleExitInpaintMode: p.handleExitInpaintMode,
    61→    handleEnterMagicEditMode: magic.handleEnterMagicEditMode,
    62→    handleExitMagicEditMode: magic.handleExitMagicEditMode,
    63→
    64→    // Brush/Inpaint
    65→    brushSize: inpainting.brushSize,
    66→    setBrushSize: inpainting.setBrushSize,
    67→    isEraseMode: inpainting.isEraseMode,
    68→    setIsEraseMode: inpainting.setIsEraseMode,
    69→    brushStrokes: inpainting.brushStrokes,
    70→
```

```
    22→interface TaskStatusCountsResult {

    36→// Hook to get status counts for indicators
    37→export const useTaskStatusCounts = (projectId: string | null) => {

    65→      // Match TasksPane list semantics: only count visible task types (and parent tasks)
    66→      const visibleTaskTypes = getVisibleTaskTypes();
    67→
    68→      // Get 1 hour ago timestamp

    70→
    71→      // Execute all queries in parallel with error resilience
    72→      const supabase = getSupabaseClient();

    81→        // Query for recent successes (last hour)

   172→                { policy: 'best_effort' },
   173→              ),
   174→      };
   175→
   176→      // [TasksPaneCountMismatch] Result snapshot to compare with list view
   177→
   178→      // Track circuit breaker - if any query failed, record failure; otherwise record success
   179→      const anyFailed = failedQueries.length > 0;
   180→
   181→      if (anyFailed) {
   182→        const errorReason = processingResult.status === 'rejected' ? processingResult.reason :
   183→                           successResult.status === 'rejected' ? successResult.reason :
   184→                           failureResult.status === 'rejected' ? failureResult.reason :
   185→                           new Error('Query returned error');
   186→        dataFreshnessManager.onFetchFailure(taskQueryKeys.statusCounts(projectId), errorReason as Error);
   187→      } else {
   188→        dataFreshnessManager.onFetchSuccess(taskQueryKeys.statusCounts(projectId));
   189→      }
   190→
   191→      return result;
   192→    },
   193→    enabled: !!projectId,
   194→    // SMART POLLING: Intelligent polling based on realtime health
   195→    ...smartPollingConfig,
   196→    refetchIntervalInBackground: true, // Enable background polling like the gallery
   197→    // Enhanced retry logic for transient network errors
   198→    retry: STANDARD_RETRY,
   199→    retryDelay: STANDARD_RETRY_DELAY,
   200→  });
   201→};
   202→
   203→/**
   204→ * Hook to get all visible task types from the config
   205→ * Simply returns the allowlist from taskConfig - no database query needed
   206→ */
   207→export const useAllTaskTypes = (_projectId: string | null) => {
   208→  return useQuery({
   209→    [REDACTED],
   210→    queryFn: () => {

   212→      const visibleTypes = getVisibleTaskTypes();
   213→      return visibleTypes;
   214→    },
   215→    // Use immutable preset - hardcoded list never changes at runtime
   216→    ...QUERY_PRESETS.immutable,
   217→    gcTime: Infinity, // Keep forever
   218→  });
   219→};
```

```
     4→import { expandShotData } from '@/shared/lib/shotData';

     6→
     7→export interface DerivedItem {
     8→  id: string;
     9→  thumbUrl: string | null;
    10→  url: string | null;
    11→  createdAt: string;
    12→  derivedCount: number;

    23→}
    24→
    25→function normalizePosition(timelineFrame: number | null | undefined): number | null {
    26→  if (timelineFrame === null || timelineFrame === undefined) {
    27→    return null;
    28→  }
    29→  return Math.floor(timelineFrame / 50);
    30→}
    31→
    32→function normalizePrompt(params: unknown): string | undefined {
    33→  const record = params as Record<string, unknown> | null;
    34→  if (!record) {
    35→    return undefined;
    36→  }
    37→
    38→  if (typeof record.prompt === 'string') {
    39→    return record.prompt;
    40→  }
    41→
    42→  const originalParams = record.originalParams as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
    43→  const orchestratorDetails = originalParams?.orchestrator_details as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
    44→  return typeof orchestratorDetails?.prompt === 'string' ? orchestratorDetails.prompt : undefined;
    45→}
    46→
    47→export async function fetchDerivedItemsFromRepository(
    48→  sourceGenerationId: string | null,
    49→): Promise<DerivedItem[]> {
    50→  if (!sourceGenerationId) {
    51→    return [];
    52→  }
    53→
    54→  const [generationsResult, variantsResult] = await Promise.all([
    55→    supabase().from('generations')
    56→      .select(`
    57→        id,
    58→        location,
    59→        thumbnail_url,
    60→        type,
    61→        created_at,
    62→        params,
    63→        starred,
    64→        tasks,
    65→        based_on,
    66→        shot_data
    67→      `)
    68→      .eq('based_on', sourceGenerationId)
    69→      .order('starred', { ascending: false, nullsFirst: false })
    70→      .order('created_at', { ascending: false }),
    71→    supabase().from('generation_variants')
    72→      .select('id, location, thumbnail_url, created_at, variant_type, name, params, is_primary, viewed_at')
    73→      .eq('generation_id', sourceGenerationId)
    74→      .in('variant_type', EDIT_VARIANT_TYPES)
    75→      .eq('is_primary', false)
    76→      .order('created_at', { ascending: false }),
    77→  ]);
    78→
    79→  if (generationsResult.error) {
    80→    normalizeAndReportError(generationsResult.error, {
    81→      context: 'generation.derivedItems.repository.generations',
    82→      showToast: false,
    83→    });
    84→  }
    85→  if (variantsResult.error) {
    86→    normalizeAndReportError(variantsResult.error, {
    87→      context: 'generation.derivedItems.repository.variants',
    88→      showToast: false,
    89→    });
    90→  }
    91→
    92→  const childGenerations = generationsResult.data || [];
    93→  const editVariants = variantsResult.data || [];
    94→
    95→  const generationIds = childGenerations.map((row) => row.id);
    96→  const { derivedCounts } = await calculateDerivedCountsSafe(generationIds);
    97→
    98→  const generationItems: DerivedItem[] = childGenerations.map((item) => {
    99→    const shotGenerations = expandShotData(
   100→      (item as { shot_data?: Record<string, unknown> | null }).shot_data,
   101→    );
   102→    const allAssociations = shotGenerations.length > 1
   103→      ? shotGenerations.map((sg) => ({
   104→          shot_id: sg.shot_id,
   105→          timeline_frame: sg.timeline_frame,
   106→          position: normalizePosition(sg.timeline_frame),
   107→        }))
   108→      : undefined;
   109→
   110→    const primaryShot = shotGenerations[0];
   111→
   112→    return {
   113→      id: item.id,
   114→      thumbUrl: item.thumbnail_url || item.location,
   115→      url: item.location,
   116→      createdAt: item.created_at,
   117→      derivedCount: derivedCounts[item.id] || 0,
   118→      starred: item.starred || false,
   119→      prompt: normalizePrompt(item.params),
   120→      itemType: 'generation',
   121→      basedOn: item.based_on,
   122→      shot_id: primaryShot?.shot_id,
   123→      timeline_frame: primaryShot?.timeline_frame,
   124→      all_shot_associations: allAssociations,
   125→    };
   126→  });
   127→
   128→  const variantItems: DerivedItem[] = editVariants.map((variant) => ({
   129→    id: variant.id,
   130→    thumbUrl: variant.thumbnail_url || variant.location,
   131→    url: variant.location,
   132→    createdAt: variant.created_at,
   133→    derivedCount: 0,
   134→    starred: false,
   135→    prompt: normalizePrompt(variant.params),
   136→    itemType: 'variant',
   137→    variantType: variant.variant_type,
   138→    variantName: variant.name,
   139→    viewedAt: variant.viewed_at,
   140→  }));
   141→
   142→  return [...generationItems, ...variantItems].sort((a, b) => {
   143→    if (a.starred && !b.starred) return -1;
   144→    if (!a.starred && b.starred) return 1;
   145→    return new Date(b.createdAt).getTime() - new Date(a.createdAt).getTime();
   146→  });
   147→}
   148→
```

```
1→import { normalizeAndReportError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandling/runtimeErrorReporting';
     2→import { getReconnectScheduler } from '@/integrations/supabase/support/reconnect/ReconnectScheduler';
     3→import type { SupabaseClient, Session } from '@supabase/supabase-js';
     4→
     5→type AuthCallback = (event: string, session: Session | null) => void;
     6→
     7→const AUTH_HEAL_DEBOUNCE_MS = 5000;
     8→
     9→export class AuthStateManager {
    10→  private listeners: Array<{id: string, callback: AuthCallback}> = [];
    11→  private isInitialized = false;
    12→  private __LAST_AUTH_HEAL_AT__ = 0;
    13→
    14→  constructor(private supabase: SupabaseClient) {}
    15→
    16→  subscribe(id: string, callback: AuthCallback) {
    17→    this.listeners.push({ id, callback });
    18→    return () => {
    19→      this.listeners = this.listeners.filter(listener => listener.id !== id);
    20→    };
    21→  }
    22→
    23→  private notifyListeners(event: string, session: Session | null) {
    24→    this.listeners.forEach(({ callback }) => {
    25→      try {
    26→        callback(event, session);
    27→      } catch (error) {
    28→        normalizeAndReportError(error, { context: 'AuthStateManager', showToast: false });
    29→      }
    30→    });
    31→  }
    32→
    33→  private handleCoreAuth(event: string, session: Session | null) {
    34→    try {
    35→      this.supabase?.realtime?.setAuth?.(session?.access_token ?? null);
    36→      
    37→      if (event === 'SIGNED_IN' && typeof window !== 'undefined') {
    38→        setTimeout(async () => {
    39→          try {
    40→            const now = Date.now();
    41→            if (now - this.__LAST_AUTH_HEAL_AT__ > AUTH_HEAL_DEBOUNCE_MS) {
    42→              this.__LAST_AUTH_HEAL_AT__ = now;
    43→              
    44→              // Use ReconnectScheduler instead of direct event dispatch
    45→              const scheduler = getReconnectScheduler();
    46→              scheduler.requestReconnect({
    47→                source: 'AuthManager',
    48→                reason: `SIGNED_IN event (${event})`,
    49→                priority: 'high'
    50→              });
    51→            }
    52→          } catch (healError) {
    53→            normalizeAndReportError(healError, { context: 'AuthStateManager', showToast: false });
    54→          }
    55→        }, 1000);
    56→      }
    57→    } catch (setAuthError) {
    58→      normalizeAndReportError(setAuthError, { context: 'AuthStateManager', showToast: false });
    59→    }
    60→  }
    61→
    62→  init() {
    63→    if (this.isInitialized) {
    64→      return;
    65→    }
    66→
    67→    try {
    68→      this.supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange((event, session) => {
    69→        this.handleCoreAuth(event, session);
    70→        this.notifyListeners(event, session);
    71→      });
    72→      this.isInitialized = true;
    73→    } catch (authError) {
    74→      normalizeAndReportError(authError, { context: 'AuthStateManager', showToast: false });
    75→    }
    76→  }
    77→}
    78→
    79→let authStateManager: AuthStateManager | null = null;
    80→
    81→export function initAuthStateManager(supabase: SupabaseClient): AuthStateManager {
    82→  if (!authStateManager) {
    83→    authStateManager = new AuthStateManager(supabase);
    84→    authStateManager.init();
    85→  }
    86→  return authStateManager;
    87→}
    88→
    89→export function getAuthStateManager(): AuthStateManager | null {
    90→  return authStateManager;
    91→}
    92→
    93→export function resetAuthStateManagerForTests(): void {
    94→  authStateManager = null;
    95→}
    96→
```

```
1→/**
     2→ * useVariantPromotion - Handles promoting variants to standalone generations
     3→ *
     4→ * Manages variant promotion (creating standalone generation from a variant)
     5→ * and adding variants as new generations to shots with timeline positioning.
     6→ */
     7→
     8→import { useState, useCallback } from 'react';
     9→import { toast } from '@/shared/components/ui/runtime/sonner';
    10→import { normalizeAndPresentError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandling/runtimeError';
    11→import { getSupabaseClient as supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
    12→import { usePromoteVariantToGeneration } from '@/shared/hooks/usePromoteVariantToGeneration';
    13→import { useAddImageToShot } from '@/shared/hooks/shots';
    14→
    15→interface UseVariantPromotionProps {
    16→  selectedProjectId: string | null;
    17→}
    18→
    19→interface UseVariantPromotionReturn {
    20→  promoteSuccess: boolean;
    21→  isPromoting: boolean;
    22→  handlePromoteToGeneration: (variantId: string) => Promise<void>;
    23→  handleAddVariantAsNewGenerationToShot: (
    24→    shotId: string,
    25→    variantId: string,
    26→    currentTimelineFrame?: number
    27→  ) => Promise<boolean>;
    28→}
    29→
    30→export function useVariantPromotion({
    31→  selectedProjectId,
    32→}: UseVariantPromotionProps): UseVariantPromotionReturn {
    33→  const promoteVariantMutation = usePromoteVariantToGeneration();
    34→  const addImageToShotMutation = useAddImageToShot();
    35→  const [promoteSuccess, setPromoteSuccess] = useState(false);
    36→
    37→  // Handler for "Make new image" button in VariantSelector
    38→  const handlePromoteToGeneration = useCallback(async (variantId: string) => {
    39→    if (!selectedProjectId) {
    40→      toast.error('No project selected');
    41→      return;
    42→    }
    43→
    44→    setPromoteSuccess(false);
    45→
    46→    try {
    47→      await promoteVariantMutation.mutateAsync({
    48→        variantId,
    49→        projectId: selectedProjectId,
    50→      });
    51→
    52→      setPromoteSuccess(true);
    53→      setTimeout(() => setPromoteSuccess(false), 2000);
    54→    } catch (error) {
    55→      normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useVariantPromotion', showToast: false });
    56→    }
    57→  }, [promoteVariantMutation, selectedProjectId]);
    58→
    59→  // Handler for "Add as new image to shot" button in ShotSelectorControls
    60→  // Positions new image between current and next item in the TARGET shot
    61→  const handleAddVariantAsNewGenerationToShot = useCallback(async (
    62→    shotId: string,
    63→    variantId: string,
    64→    currentTimelineFrame?: number
    65→  ): Promise<boolean> => {
    66→    if (!selectedProjectId) {
    67→      toast.error('No project selected');
    68→      return false;
    69→    }
    70→
    71→    try {
    72→      // 1. Create the generation from the variant
    73→      const newGen = await promoteVariantMutation.mutateAsync({
    74→        variantId,
    75→        projectId: selectedProjectId,
    76→      });
    77→
    78→      // 2. Calculate target timeline frame by querying the TARGET shot's items
    79→      let targetTimelineFrame: number | undefined;
    80→      if (currentTimelineFrame !== undefined) {
    81→        // Query all items in the target shot to find next item and calculate average spacing
    82→        const { data: allShotItems } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
    83→          .select('timeline_frame')
    84→          .eq('shot_id', shotId)
    85→          .not('timeline_frame', 'is', null)
    86→          .order('timeline_frame', { ascending: true });
    87→
    88→        const frames = (allShotItems || [])
    89→          .map(item => item.timeline_frame as number)
    90→          .filter(f => f !== null && f !== undefined);
    91→
    92→        // Find the next item after current position
    93→        const nextTimelineFrame = frames.find(f => f > currentTimelineFrame);
    94→
    95→        if (nextTimelineFrame !== undefined && nextTimelineFrame > currentTimelineFrame) {
    96→          // Place in the middle between current and next
    97→          targetTimelineFrame = Math.floor((currentTimelineFrame + nextTimelineFrame) / 2);
    98→          // If middle would be same as current (consecutive frames), use current + 1
    99→          if (targetTimelineFrame === currentTimelineFrame) {
   100→            targetTimelineFrame = currentTimelineFrame + 1;
   101→          }
   102→        } else {
   103→          // No next item in shot - calculate average spacing and use that
   104→          if (frames.length >= 2) {
   105→            // Calculate average gap between consecutive frames
   106→            let totalGap = 0;
   107→            for (let i = 1; i < frames.length; i++) {
   108→              totalGap += frames[i] - frames[i - 1];
   109→            }
   110→            const averageGap = Math.round(totalGap / (frames.length - 1));
   111→            targetTimelineFrame = currentTimelineFrame + Math.max(1, averageGap);
   112→          } else {
   113→            // Only one item in shot, use current + 1
   114→            targetTimelineFrame = currentTimelineFrame + 1;
   115→          }
   116→        }
   117→      }
   118→
   119→      // 3. Add to shot
   120→      await addImageToShotMutation.mutateAsync({
   121→        shot_id: shotId,
   122→        generation_id: newGen.id,
   123→        project_id: selectedProjectId,
   124→        imageUrl: newGen.location,
   125→        thumbUrl: newGen.thumbnail_url || undefined,
   126→        timelineFrame: targetTimelineFrame,
   127→      });
   128→      return true;
   129→    } catch (error) {
   130→      normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useVariantPromotion', showToast: false });
   131→      return false;
   132→    }
   133→  }, [promoteVariantMutation, addImageToShotMutation, selectedProjectId]);
   134→
   135→  return {
   136→    promoteSuccess,
   137→    isPromoting: promoteVariantMutation.isPending,
   138→    handlePromoteToGeneration,
   139→    handleAddVariantAsNewGenerationToShot,
   140→  };
   141→}
   142→
```

```
1→/**
     2→ * useReplaceInShot Hook
     3→ *
     4→ * Handles swapping timeline position from a parent generation to the current image.
     5→ * Used when user wants to replace a parent image in the timeline with a derived image.
     6→ */
     7→
     8→import { useCallback } from 'react';
     9→import { normalizeAndPresentError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandling/runtimeError';
    10→import { getSupabaseClient as supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
    11→
    12→interface UseReplaceInShotProps {
    13→  /** Callback to close the lightbox after successful replacement */
    14→  onClose: () => void;
    15→}
    16→
    17→interface UseReplaceInShotReturn {
    18→  /**
    19→   * Replace parent's timeline position with current image
    20→   * @param parentGenerationId - ID of the parent generation to remove from timeline
    21→   * @param currentMediaId - ID of the current media to place in timeline
    22→   * @param parentTimelineFrame - Timeline frame position to use
    23→   * @param shotId - Shot ID for the replacement
    24→   */
    25→  handleReplaceInShot: (
    26→    parentGenerationId: string,
    27→    currentMediaId: string,
    28→    parentTimelineFrame: number,
    29→    shotId: string
    30→  ) => Promise<void>;
    31→}
    32→
    33→export function useReplaceInShot({
    34→  onClose,
    35→}: UseReplaceInShotProps): UseReplaceInShotReturn {
    36→  const handleReplaceInShot = useCallback(async (
    37→    parentGenerationId: string,
    38→    currentMediaId: string,
    39→    parentTimelineFrame: number,
    40→    shotIdParam: string
    41→  ) => {
    42→
    43→    try {
    44→      // 1. Remove timeline_frame from parent's shot_generation record
    45→      const { error: removeError } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
    46→        .update({ timeline_frame: null })
    47→        .eq('generation_id', parentGenerationId)
    48→        .eq('shot_id', shotIdParam);
    49→
    50→      if (removeError) throw removeError;
    51→
    52→      // 2. Update or create shot_generation for current image with the timeline_frame
    53→      // First check if current image already has a shot_generation for this shot
    54→      const { data: existingAssoc } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
    55→        .select('id')
    56→        .eq('generation_id', currentMediaId)
    57→        .eq('shot_id', shotIdParam)
    58→        .single();
    59→
    60→      if (existingAssoc) {
    61→        // Update existing
    62→        const { error: updateError } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
    63→          .update({
    64→            timeline_frame: parentTimelineFrame,
    65→            metadata: { user_positioned: true, drag_source: 'replace_parent' }
    66→          })
    67→          .eq('id', existingAssoc.id);
    68→
    69→        if (updateError) throw updateError;
    70→      } else {
    71→        // Create new
    72→        const { error: createError } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
    73→          .insert({
    74→            shot_id: shotIdParam,
    75→            generation_id: currentMediaId,
    76→            timeline_frame: parentTimelineFrame,
    77→            metadata: { user_positioned: true, drag_source: 'replace_parent' }
    78→          });
    79→
    80→        if (createError) throw createError;
    81→      }
    82→
    83→      // Close lightbox to force refresh when reopened
    84→      onClose();
    85→    } catch (error) {
    86→      normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useReplaceInShot', showToast: false });
    87→      throw error;
    88→    }
    89→  }, [onClose]);
    90→
    91→  return { handleReplaceInShot };
    92→}
    93→
```

```
    89→async function waitForVariantDelay(
```

```
1→/**
     2→ * RealtimeConnection - Manages Supabase WebSocket connection lifecycle
     3→ *
     4→ * Single responsibility: Connect, reconnect, and emit connection status changes.
     5→ * Does NOT filter events or make business decisions about what to invalidate.
     6→ *
     7→ * State machine: disconnected → connecting → connected ↔ reconnecting → failed
     8→ */
     9→
    10→import { RealtimeChannel } from '@supabase/supabase-js';
    11→import {
    12→  createRealtimeChannel,

    32→export class RealtimeConnection {

    35→  private config: RealtimeConfig;
    36→
    37→  private reconnectTimeout: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;
    38→  private subscribeTimeout: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;
    39→
    40→  private statusCallbacks = new Set<ConnectionStatusCallback>();
    41→  private eventCallbacks = new Set<RawEventCallback>();
    42→  private unsubAuthHeal: (() => void) | null = null;
    43→  private activeConnectSequence = 0;
    44→  private connectInFlight: Promise<boolean> | null = null;
    45→  private connectInFlightProjectId: string | null = null;
    46→
    47→  constructor(config: Partial<RealtimeConfig> = {}) {
    48→    this.config = { ...DEFAULT_REALTIME_CONFIG, ...config };
    49→
    50→    // Listen for auth heal events
    51→    if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
    52→      this.unsubAuthHeal = listenAppEvent('realtime:auth-heal', () => this.handleAuthHeal());
    53→    }
    54→  }
    55→
    56→  // ===========================================================================
    57→  // Public API
    58→  // ===========================================================================
    59→
    60→  /**
    61→   * Connect to a project's realtime channel.
    62→   * If already connected to a different project, disconnects first.
    63→   */
    64→  async connect(projectId: string): Promise<boolean> {
    65→    // If connecting to same project and already connected, no-op
    66→    if (this.state.projectId === projectId && this.state.status === 'connected') {
    67→      return true;
    68→    }
    69→
    70→    // If connecting to different project, disconnect first
    71→    if (this.state.projectId && this.state.projectId !== projectId) {
    72→      await this.disconnect();
    73→    }
    74→
    75→    return this.startConnect(projectId);
    76→  }
```

```
    13→export function parseTaskParams(params: string | Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined): Record<string, unknown> {

    40→    if (travelImages.length > 0) {
    41→      return travelImages;

    44→
    45→  const orchestratorDetails = asRecord(params.orchestrator_details);

    47→  const segmentParams = asRecord(params.individual_segment_params);

    50→  const isSegmentTask = params?.segment_index !== undefined;
    51→
    52→  // For segment tasks, ONLY use segment-specific images (not the full orchestrator list)
    53→  if (isSegmentTask) {
    54→    // Priority: individual_segment_params > top-level input_image_paths_resolved
    55→    if (Array.isArray(segmentParams?.input_image_paths_resolved) && segmentParams.input_image_paths_resolved.length > 0) {
    56→      return segmentParams.input_image_paths_resolved.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === 'string');
    57→    }
    58→    // Fallback to start/end image URLs
    59→    if (segmentParams?.start_image_url || segmentParams?.end_image_url) {
    60→      const urls: string[] = [];
    61→      if (typeof segmentParams?.start_image_url === 'string') urls.push(segmentParams.start_image_url);
    62→      if (typeof segmentParams?.end_image_url === 'string') urls.push(segmentParams.end_image_url);
    63→      return urls;
    64→    }
    65→    // Fallback to top-level (which should be segment-specific for segment tasks)
    66→    if (Array.isArray(params?.input_image_paths_resolved)) {

    68→    }

    77→  if (typeof params?.image === 'string') urls.push(params.image);
    78→  if (typeof params?.input_image === 'string') urls.push(params.input_image);
    79→  if (typeof params?.init_image === 'string') urls.push(params.init_image);
    80→  if (typeof params?.control_image === 'string') urls.push(params.control_image);
    81→  if (Array.isArray(params?.images)) urls.push(...params.images.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === 'string'));
    82→  if (Array.isArray(params?.input_images)) urls.push(...params.input_images.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === 'string'));
    83→  if (typeof params?.mask_url === 'string') urls.push(params.mask_url);
    84→
    85→  // Travel/video task paths - orchestrator details contain all images for full timeline
    86→  if (Array.isArray(orchestratorDetails?.input_image_paths_resolved)) {
    87→    urls.push(...orchestratorDetails.input_image_paths_resolved.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === 'string'));
    88→  } else if (Array.isArray(orchestratorPayload?.input_image_paths_resolved)) {
    89→    urls.push(...orchestratorPayload.input_image_paths_resolved.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === 'string'));
    90→  } else if (Array.isArray(params?.input_image_paths_resolved)) {
    91→    urls.push(...params.input_image_paths_resolved.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === 'string'));
    92→  }

    94→  return Array.from(new Set(urls.filter(Boolean)));
    95→}
    96→
    97→/**
    98→ * Extract prompt from task params
    99→ *
   100→ * For segment tasks: Checks individual_segment_params first
   101→ * For orchestrated tasks: Checks orchestrator details
   102→ * For other tasks: Falls back to top-level prompt
   103→ *
   104→ * Prefers enhanced_prompts_expanded over base_prompts_expanded when available,
   105→ * as enhanced prompts contain the AI-improved version of the user's prompt.
   106→ *
   107→ * @param parsedParams - Already-parsed task params object
   108→ * @returns The prompt string or null
   109→ */
   110→export function derivePrompt(parsedParams: Record<string, unknown>): string | null {
   111→  const params = parsedParams;
   112→  if (isTravelTaskParams(params)) {
   113→    return deriveTravelPrompt(params);
   114→  }
   115→
   116→  const orchestratorDetails = asRecord(params.orchestrator_details);
   117→  const orchestratorPayload = asRecord(params.full_orchestrator_payload);
   118→  const segmentParams = asRecord(params.individual_segment_params);
   119→  const segmentIndex = toIntegerOrNull(params.segment_index);
   120→
   121→  const isSegmentTask = params.segment_index !== undefined;
   122→
   123→  // For segment tasks, try to get enhanced prompt first
   124→  if (isSegmentTask) {
   125→    // Check for enhanced prompt - can be singular field or in expanded array
   126→    const enhancedFromOrchestratorDetails = asStringArray(orchestratorDetails?.enhanced_prompts_expanded);
   127→    const enhancedFromOrchestratorPayload = asStringArray(orchestratorPayload?.enhanced_prompts_expanded);
   128→    const enhancedPrompt = pickFirstString(
   129→      segmentParams?.enhanced_prompt,
   130→      params.enhanced_prompt,
   131→      segmentIndex === null ? undefined : enhancedFromOrchestratorDetails?.[segmentIndex],
   132→      segmentIndex === null ? undefined : enhancedFromOrchestratorPayload?.[segmentIndex],
   133→    );
   134→    if (enhancedPrompt) return enhancedPrompt;
   135→
   136→    // Fall back to base prompt
   137→    return (
   138→      pickFirstString(
   139→        segmentParams?.base_prompt,
   140→        params.base_prompt,
   141→        params.prompt,
   142→        orchestratorDetails?.base_prompt,
   143→      ) ?? null
   144→    );
   145→  }
   146→
   147→  // For full timeline/orchestrated tasks
   148→  // The global base_prompt is what the user typed in the prompt field.
   149→  // Per-pair overrides (base_prompts_expanded) are segment-specific and shouldn't
   150→  // be shown as the task-level prompt — they're misleading when the user explicitly
   151→  // cleared the global prompt.
   152→  const enhancedFromOrchestratorDetails = asStringArray(orchestratorDetails?.enhanced_prompts_expanded);
   153→  const enhancedFromOrchestratorPayload = asStringArray(orchestratorPayload?.enhanced_prompts_expanded);
   154→  return (
   155→    pickFirstString(
   156→      orchestratorDetails?.base_prompt,
   157→      orchestratorPayload?.base_prompt,
   158→      params.base_prompt,
   159→      params.prompt,
   160→      // Fall back to enhanced prompts (AI-improved) but NOT base_prompts_expanded
   161→      // which are per-pair overrides, not task-level prompts.
   162→      enhancedFromOrchestratorDetails?.[0],
   163→      enhancedFromOrchestratorPayload?.[0],
   164→    ) ?? null
   165→  );
   166→}
   167→
   168→/**
   169→ * Check if a task type is an image edit task
   170→ */
   171→export function isImageEditTaskType(taskType: string | undefined): boolean {
   172→  const IMAGE_EDIT_TASK_TYPES = [
   173→    'z_image_turbo_i2i',
   174→    'image_inpaint',
   175→    'qwen_image_edit',
   176→    'magic_edit',
   177→    'kontext_image_edit',
   178→    'flux_image_edit',
   179→    'annotated_image_edit',
   180→  ];
   181→  return IMAGE_EDIT_TASK_TYPES.includes(taskType || '');
   182→}
   183→
   184→/**
   185→ * Check if a task type is a video enhancement task
   186→ */
   187→export function isVideoEnhanceTaskType(taskType: string | undefined): boolean {
   188→  return taskType === 'video_enhance';
   189→}
   190→
   191→/**
   192→ * Check if a task type is an image enhancement/upscale task
   193→ */
   194→export function isImageEnhanceTaskType(taskType: string | undefined): boolean {
   195→  return taskType === 'image-upscale';
   196→}
   197→
   198→/**
   199→ * LoRA info extracted from task params
   200→ */
   201→interface LoraInfo {
   202→  url: string;
   203→  strength: number;
   204→  displayName: string;
   205→}
   206→
   207→/**
   208→ * Extract LoRAs from task params (checks multiple locations)
   209→ */
   210→export function extractLoras(parsedParams: Record<string, unknown>): LoraInfo[] {
   211→  const params = parsedParams;
   212→  const orchestratorDetails = asRecord(params.orchestrator_details);
   213→  const orchestratorPayload = asRecord(params.full_orchestrator_payload);
   214→
   215→  // Check for array format (image edit tasks use this)
   216→  const lorasArray = params.loras || orchestratorDetails?.loras || orchestratorPayload?.loras;
   217→  if (Array.isArray(lorasArray) && lorasArray.length > 0) {
   218→    return lorasArray
   219→      .map((lora): LoraInfo | null => {
   220→        const loraRecord = asRecord(lora);
   221→        if (!loraRecord) return null;
   222→        const url = asString(loraRecord.url) ?? '';
   223→        const parsedStrength = toFiniteNumber(loraRecord.strength) ?? toFiniteNumber(loraRecord.multiplier) ?? 1;
   224→        return {
   225→          url,
   226→          strength: parsedStrength,
   227→          displayName: extractLoraDisplayName(url),
   228→        };
   229→      })
   230→      .filter((lora): lora is LoraInfo => lora !== null);
   231→  }
   232→
   233→  // Check for object format (video tasks use additional_loras)
   234→  const additionalLoras = params.additional_loras || orchestratorDetails?.additional_loras || orchestratorPayload?.additional_loras;
   235→  if (additionalLoras && typeof additionalLoras === 'object' && Object.keys(additionalLoras as Record<string, unknown>).length > 0) {
   236→    return Object.entries(additionalLoras as Record<string, unknown>).map(([url, strength]) => ({
   237→      url,
   238→      strength: toFiniteNumber(strength) ?? 1,
   239→      displayName: extractLoraDisplayName(url),
   240→    }));
   241→  }
   242→
   243→  return [];
   244→}
   245→
   246→function extractLoraDisplayName(url: string): string {
   247→  const fileName = url.split('/').pop() || 'Unknown';
   248→  return fileName.replace(/\.(safetensors|ckpt|pt)$/i, '').replace(/_/g, ' ');
   249→}
   250→
   251→const TRAVEL_SEGMENT_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER: TravelPayloadSource[] = [
   252→  'individualSegmentParams',
   253→  'taskViewContract',
   254→  'familyContract',
   255→  'rawParams',
   256→];
   257→
   258→const TRAVEL_TIMELINE_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER: TravelPayloadSource[] = [
   259→  'taskViewContract',
   260→  'familyContract',
   261→  'orchestratorDetails',
   262→  'fullOrchestratorPayload',
   263→  'rawParams',
   264→];
   265→
   266→const TRAVEL_PROMPT_SOURCE_ORDER: TravelPayloadSource[] = [
   267→  'taskViewContract',
   268→  'familyContract',
   269→  'individualSegmentParams',
   270→  'orchestratorDetails',
   271→  'fullOrchestratorPayload',
   272→  'rawParams',
   273→];
   274→
   275→function dedupeTruthyStrings(values: Array<string | undefined>): string[] {
   276→  return Array.from(new Set(values.filter((value): value is string => typeof value === 'string' && value.length > 0)));
   277→}
   278→
   279→function isTravelTaskParams(params: Record<string, unknown>): boolean {
   280→  const familyContract = asRecord(params.task_family_contract);
   281→  return (
   282→    params.task_family === 'travel_between_images'
   283→    || familyContract?.task_family === 'travel_between_images'
   284→    || params.orchestrator_details !== undefined
   285→    || params.full_orchestrator_payload !== undefined
   286→    || params.individual_segment_params !== undefined
   287→    || Array.isArray(params.image_urls)
   288→    || Array.isArray(params.input_image_paths_resolved)
   289→  );
   290→}
   291→
   292→function deriveTravelInputImages(params: Record<string, unknown>): string[] {
   293→  const snapshot = buildTaskPayloadSnapshot(params);
   294→  const reader = createTravelPayloadReader(snapshot);
   295→  const isSegmentTask = params.segment_index !== undefined;
   296→
   297→  if (isSegmentTask) {
   298→    const segmentInputImages = reader.pickStringArray('input_image_paths_resolved', TRAVEL_SEGMENT_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER);
   299→    if (segmentInputImages && segmentInputImages.length > 0) {
   300→      return dedupeTruthyStrings(segmentInputImages);
   301→    }
   302→
   303→    const startImage = reader.pickString('start_image_url', TRAVEL_SEGMENT_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER);
   304→    const endImage = reader.pickString('end_image_url', TRAVEL_SEGMENT_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER);
   305→    return dedupeTruthyStrings([startImage, endImage]);
   306→  }
   307→
   308→  const timelineSources = [
   309→    reader.pickStringArray('input_images', TRAVEL_TIMELINE_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER),
   310→    reader.pickStringArray('input_image_paths_resolved', TRAVEL_TIMELINE_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER),
   311→    reader.pickStringArray('image_urls', TRAVEL_TIMELINE_IMAGE_SOURCE_ORDER),
   312→  ];
   313→  for (const candidate of timelineSources) {
   314→    if (candidate && candidate.length > 0) {
   315→      return dedupeTruthyStrings(candidate);
   316→    }
   317→  }
   318→
   319→  return [];
   320→}
   321→
   322→function deriveTravelPrompt(params: Record<string, unknown>): string | null {
   323→  const snapshot = buildTaskPayloadSnapshot(params);
   324→  const reader = createTravelPayloadReader(snapshot);
   325→  const segmentIndex = toIntegerOrNull(params.segment_index);
   326→  const isSegmentTask = params.segment_index !== undefined;
   327→
   328→  if (isSegmentTask) {
   329→    const enhancedPromptsExpanded = reader.pickStringArray('enhanced_prompts_expanded', [
   330→      'orchestratorDetails',
   331→      'fullOrchestratorPayload',
   332→      'rawParams',
   333→    ]);
   334→    const enhancedPrompt = pickFirstString(
   335→      reader.pickString('enhanced_prompt', TRAVEL_PROMPT_SOURCE_ORDER),
   336→      segmentIndex === null ? undefined : enhancedPromptsExpanded?.[segmentIndex],
   337→    );
   338→    if (enhancedPrompt) {
   339→      return enhancedPrompt;
   340→    }
   341→
   342→    return (
   343→      pickFirstString(
   344→        reader.pickString('prompt', TRAVEL_PROMPT_SOURCE_ORDER),
   345→        reader.pickString('base_prompt', TRAVEL_PROMPT_SOURCE_ORDER),
   346→      ) ?? null
   347→    );
   348→  }
   349→
   350→  return (
   351→    pickFirstString(
   352→      reader.pickString('prompt', TRAVEL_PROMPT_SOURCE_ORDER),
   353→      reader.pickString('base_prompt', TRAVEL_PROMPT_SOURCE_ORDER),
   354→      reader.pickString('enhanced_prompt', TRAVEL_PROMPT_SOURCE_ORDER),
   355→    ) ?? null
   356→  );
   357→}
   358→
   359→function asRecord(value: unknown): Record<string, unknown> | null {
   360→  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object' || Array.isArray(value)) return null;
   361→  return value as Record<string, unknown>;
   362→}
   363→
   364→function asString(value: unknown): string | null {
   365→  return typeof value === 'string' ? value : null;
   366→}
   367→
   368→function asStringArray(value: unknown): string[] | null {
   369→  if (!Array.isArray(value)) return null;
   370→  return value.filter((item): item is string => typeof item === 'string');
   371→}
   372→
   373→function toIntegerOrNull(value: unknown): number | null {
   374→  const numeric = toFiniteNumber(value);
   375→  if (numeric === null || !Number.isInteger(numeric)) return null;
   376→  return numeric;
   377→}
   378→
   379→function toFiniteNumber(value: unknown): number | null {
   380→  const numeric = typeof value === 'number' ? value : Number(value);
   381→  return Number.isFinite(numeric) ? numeric : null;
   382→}
   383→
   384→function pickFirstString(...values: unknown[]): string | null {
   385→  for (const value of values) {
   386→    const text = asString(value);
   387→    if (text) return text;
   388→  }
   389→  return null;
   390→}
```

```
1→// Supabase config is intentionally lazy: importing this module should not throw.
     2→// Env validation happens only when callers access URL/key getters.
     3→//
     4→// Migration contract for legacy constant removal:
     5→// - Owner: platform-foundations
     6→// - Remove-by: 2026-05-31
     7→// - Gate: no remaining imports of old SUPABASE_URL/SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY symbols
     8→
     9→function requireEnv(name: string): string {
    10→  const value = import.meta.env[name] as string | undefined;
    11→  if (!value) {
    12→    throw new Error(`Missing required Supabase environment variable: ${name}`);
    13→  }
    14→  return value;
    15→}
    16→
    17→function getBooleanEnv(name: string, fallback: boolean): boolean {
    18→  const value = import.meta.env[name] as string | undefined;
    19→  if (value === undefined) return fallback;
    20→  if (value === 'true' || value === '1') return true;
    21→  if (value === 'false' || value === '0') return false;
    22→  return fallback;
    23→}
    24→
    25→let _supabaseUrl: string | undefined;
    26→/** Supabase project URL — throws on first access if VITE_SUPABASE_URL is missing. */
    27→export function getSupabaseUrl(): string {
```

```
   172→
   173→        xhr.addEventListener('abort', () => {
   174→          cleanup();
   175→          signal?.removeEventListener('abort', abortHandler);
   176→          // Reject if not already rejected by timeout/stall/signal handlers
   177→          reject(new Error('Upload aborted'));
   178→        });
   179→
   180→        xhr.open('POST', bucketUrl);
   181→        xhr.setRequestHeader('Authorization', `Bearer ${accessToken}`);
   182→        xhr.setRequestHeader('Content-Type', file.type || 'video/mp4');
   183→        xhr.setRequestHeader('Cache-Control', '3600');
   184→
   185→        xhr.send(file);
   186→      });
   187→
   188→      // Get public URL
   189→      const { data: { publicUrl } } = supabase().storage
   190→        .from(MEDIA_BUCKET)
   191→        .getPublicUrl(fileName);
   192→
   193→      return publicUrl;
   194→
   195→    } catch (error) {
   196→      lastError = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error('Unknown upload error');
   197→      normalizeAndPresentError(lastError, { context: 'VideoUploader', showToast: false });
   198→
   199→      // Don't retry for user cancellation
   200→      if (lastError.message.includes('cancelled')) {
   201→        throw lastError;
   202→      }
   203→
   204→      if (attempt < maxRetries - 1) {
   205→        // Wait before retrying (exponential backoff)
   206→        const delay = Math.pow(2, attempt) * 1000;
   207→        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, delay));
   208→      }
   209→    }
   210→  }
   211→
   212→  // Provide more specific error messages
   213→  if (lastError?.message.includes('cancelled')) {
   214→    throw new Error('Upload cancelled');
   215→  } else if (lastError?.message.includes('timed out') || lastError?.message.includes('stalled')) {
   216→    throw new Error(`Video upload failed: ${file.name} (${fileSizeMB}MB) - connection too slow or unstable. Please check your connection and try again.`);
   217→  } else {
   218→    throw lastError || new Error('Failed to upload video after multiple attempts');
   219→  }
```

```
    27→_HEX8_RE = re.compile(r'^[0-9a-f]{8}$')
    28→
    29→
    30→def _suggest_close_matches(state: dict, plan: dict | None, patterns: list[str]) -> None:
    31→    """Print fuzzy match suggestions for patterns that resolved to zero issues."""
    32→    all_ids: list[str] = list(state.get("issues", {}).keys())
    33→    if plan is not None:
    34→        seen_ids: set[str] = set(all_ids)
    35→        for fid in plan.get("queue_order", []):
    36→            if fid not in seen_ids:
    37→                seen_ids.add(fid)
    38→                all_ids.append(fid)
    39→        for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
    40→            for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", []):
    41→                if fid not in seen_ids:
    42→                    seen_ids.add(fid)
    43→                    all_ids.append(fid)
    44→
    45→    for pattern in patterns:
    46→        segments = pattern.split("::")
    47→        last_seg = segments[-1]
    48→        suggestions: list[str] = []
    49→
    50→        if _HEX8_RE.match(last_seg):
    51→            suggestions = [fid for fid in all_ids if fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}") or fid == last_seg]
    52→            if suggestions:
    53→                print(colorize(f"  No match for: {pattern!r}", "yellow"))
    54→                print(colorize("  Did you mean:", "dim"))
    55→                for m in suggestions[:3]:
    56→                    print(colorize(f"    {m}", "dim"))
    57→                print(colorize(f"  Tip: match by hash suffix alone: {last_seg}", "dim"))
    58→            continue
    59→
    60→        # Try last segment and second-to-last as descriptive name slugs
    61→        slug = segments[-2] if len(segments) >= 2 else ""
    62→        for fid in all_ids:
    63→            if f"::{last_seg}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}"):
    64→                suggestions.append(fid)
    65→            elif slug and (f"::{slug}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{slug}")):
    66→                suggestions.append(fid)
    67→        if suggestions:
    68→            print(colorize(f"  No match for: {pattern!r}", "yellow"))
    69→            print(colorize("  Did you mean:", "dim"))
    70→            for m in suggestions[:3]:
    71→                print(colorize(f"    {m}", "dim"))
    72→
    73→
    74→def _print_pattern_hints() -> None:
    75→    """Print valid pattern format hints after a no-match error.
    76→
    77→    Side-effect only: prints help text to stdout when pattern resolution
    78→    returns zero matches, guiding the user toward valid pattern syntax.
    79→    """
    80→    print(colorize("  Valid patterns:", "dim"))
    81→    print(colorize("    f41b3eb7              (8-char hash suffix from dashboard)", "dim"))
    82→    print(colorize("    review::path::name    (ID prefix)", "dim"))
    83→    print(colorize("    review                (all issues from detector)", "dim"))
    84→    print(colorize("    src/foo.py            (all issues in file)", "dim"))
    85→    print(colorize("    timing_attack         (issue name — last ::segment of ID)", "dim"))
    86→    print(colorize("    review::*naming*      (glob pattern)", "dim"))
    87→    print(colorize("    my-cluster            (cluster name — expands to members)", "dim"))
    88→

   108→def _cmd_cluster_add(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   109→    state = command_runtime(args).state
   110→    if not require_completed_scan(state):
   111→        return
   112→
   113→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   114→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   115→    dry_run: bool = getattr(args, "dry_run", False)
   116→
   117→    plan = load_plan()
   118→    issue_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, patterns, plan=plan)
   119→    if not issue_ids:
   120→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found.", "yellow"))
   121→        _print_pattern_hints()
   122→        _suggest_close_matches(state, plan, patterns)
   123→        return
   124→
   125→    if dry_run:
   126→        print(colorize(f"  [dry-run] Would add {len(issue_ids)} item(s) to {cluster_name}:", "cyan"))
   127→        for fid in issue_ids:
   128→            print(colorize(f"    {fid}", "dim"))
   129→        return
   130→
   131→    try:
   132→        count = add_to_cluster(plan, cluster_name, issue_ids)
   133→    except ValueError as ex:
   134→        print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   135→        return
   136→
   137→    # Check for overlap with other manual clusters
   138→    member_set = set(issue_ids)
   139→    for other_name, other_cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   140→        if other_name == cluster_name or other_cluster.get("auto"):
   141→            continue
   142→        other_ids = set(other_cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   143→        if not other_ids:
   144→            continue
   145→        overlap = member_set & other_ids
   146→        if len(overlap) > len(other_ids) * 0.5:
   147→            print(colorize(
   148→                f"  Warning: {len(overlap)} issue(s) also in cluster '{other_name}' "
   149→                f"({len(overlap)}/{len(other_ids)} = {int(len(overlap)/len(other_ids)*100)}% overlap).",
   150→                "yellow",
   151→            ))
   152→
   153→    append_log_entry(
   154→        plan, "cluster_add", issue_ids=issue_ids, cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   155→    )
   156→    save_plan(plan)
   157→    print(colorize(f"  Added {count} item(s) to cluster {cluster_name}.", "green"))

   210→def _resolve_item_position(
   211→    position: str,
   212→    target: str | None,
   213→    item_ids: list[str],
   214→    ordered_slice: list[str],
   215→    cluster_member_set: set[str],
   216→    cluster_name: str,
   217→    state: dict,
   218→    plan: dict,
   219→) -> tuple[str, str | None, int | None] | None:
   220→    """Resolve where items should be positioned within a cluster.
   221→
   222→    Returns (resolved_position, resolved_target, offset) on success,
   223→    or None if an error was printed and the caller should abort.
   224→    """
   225→    item_set = set(item_ids)
   226→
   227→    if position == "top":
   228→        first_non_item = next((fid for fid in ordered_slice if fid not in item_set), None)
   229→        if first_non_item is None or set(ordered_slice[:len(item_ids)]) == item_set:
   230→            print(colorize("  Already at the top of the cluster.", "yellow"))
   231→            return None
   232→        return ("before", first_non_item, None)
   233→
   234→    if position == "bottom":
   235→        last_non_item = next((fid for fid in reversed(ordered_slice) if fid not in item_set), None)
   236→        if last_non_item is None or set(ordered_slice[-len(item_ids):]) == item_set:
   237→            print(colorize("  Already at the bottom of the cluster.", "yellow"))
   238→            return None
   239→        return ("after", last_non_item, None)
   240→
   241→    if position in ("before", "after"):
   242→        if target is None:
   243→            print(colorize(f"  '{position}' requires a target. Example: --item PAT {position} TARGET", "red"))
   244→            return None
   245→        target_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, [target], plan=plan)
   246→        if not target_ids:
   247→            print(colorize(f"  No match for target {target!r}.", "yellow"))
   248→            return None
   249→        resolved_target = target_ids[0]
   250→        if resolved_target not in cluster_member_set:
   251→            print(colorize(f"  Target {resolved_target!r} is not in cluster {cluster_name!r}.", "red"))
   252→            return None
   253→        return (position, resolved_target, None)
   254→
   255→    if position in ("up", "down"):
   256→        if target is None:
   257→            print(colorize(f"  '{position}' requires an offset. Example: --item PAT {position} 3", "red"))
   258→            return None
   259→        try:
   260→            offset = int(target)
   261→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   262→            print(colorize(f"  Invalid offset: {target}", "red"))
   263→            return None
   264→        return (position, None, offset)
   265→
   266→    return (position, None, None)
   267→
   268→
   269→def _reorder_within_cluster(
   270→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   271→    plan: dict,
   272→    clusters: dict,
   273→    cluster_names: list[str],
   274→    position: str,
   275→    target: str | None,
   276→    item_pattern: str,
   277→) -> None:
   278→    """Reorder items within a single cluster."""
   279→    if len(cluster_names) != 1:
   280→        print(colorize("  --item requires exactly one cluster name.", "red"))
   281→        return
   282→    cluster_name = cluster_names[0]
   283→    cluster_member_set = set(clusters[cluster_name].get("issue_ids", []))
   284→
   285→    state = command_runtime(args).state
   286→    item_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, [item_pattern], plan=plan)
   287→    if not item_ids:
   288→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found for --item pattern.", "yellow"))
   289→        return
   290→    for fid in item_ids:
   291→        if fid not in cluster_member_set:
   292→            print(colorize(f"  {fid!r} is not a member of cluster {cluster_name!r}.", "red"))
   293→            return
   294→
   295→    queue_order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   296→    ordered_slice = [fid for fid in queue_order if fid in cluster_member_set]
   297→
   298→    result = _resolve_item_position(
   299→        position, target, item_ids, ordered_slice,
   300→        cluster_member_set, cluster_name, state, plan,
   301→    )
   302→    if result is None:
   303→        return
   304→    resolved_position, resolved_target, offset = result
   305→
   306→    count = move_items(plan, item_ids, resolved_position, target=resolved_target, offset=offset)
   307→    append_log_entry(
   308→        plan, "cluster_reorder", cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   309→        detail={"position": resolved_position, "count": count, "item": item_pattern},
   310→    )
   311→    save_plan(plan)
   312→    print(colorize(f"  Moved {count} item(s) to {resolved_position} within cluster {cluster_name}.", "green"))
   313→
   314→
   315→def _reorder_whole_clusters(
   316→    plan: dict,
   317→    clusters: dict,
   318→    cluster_names: list[str],
   319→    position: str,
   320→    target: str | None,
   321→) -> None:
   322→    """Reorder entire clusters as blocks relative to each other."""
   323→    target = resolve_target(plan, target, position)
   324→
   325→    offset = None
   326→    if position in ("up", "down") and target is not None:
   327→        try:
   328→            offset = int(target)
   329→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   330→            print(colorize(f"  Invalid offset: {target}", "red"))
   331→            return
   332→        target = None
   333→
   334→    seen: set[str] = set()
   335→    all_member_ids: list[str] = []
   336→    for name in cluster_names:
   337→        for fid in clusters[name].get("issue_ids", []):
   338→            if fid not in seen:
   339→                seen.add(fid)
   340→                all_member_ids.append(fid)
   341→
   342→    if not all_member_ids:
   343→        print(colorize("  No members in the specified cluster(s).", "yellow"))
   344→        return
   345→
   346→    count = move_items(plan, all_member_ids, position, target=target, offset=offset)
   347→    append_log_entry(
   348→        plan, "cluster_reorder", cluster_name=",".join(cluster_names), actor="user",
   349→        detail={"position": position, "count": count},
   350→    )
   351→    save_plan(plan)
   352→    label = ", ".join(cluster_names)
   353→    print(colorize(f"  Moved cluster(s) {label} ({count} items) to {position}.", "green"))
   354→
   355→
   356→def _cmd_cluster_reorder(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   357→    raw_names: str = getattr(args, "cluster_names", "") or getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   358→    cluster_names: list[str] = [n.strip() for n in raw_names.split(",") if n.strip()]
   359→    position: str = getattr(args, "position", "top")
   360→    target: str | None = getattr(args, "target", None)
   361→    item_pattern: str | None = getattr(args, "item_pattern", None)
   362→
   363→    plan = load_plan()
   364→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   365→
   366→    # Validate all names exist
   367→    for name in cluster_names:
   368→        if name not in clusters:
   369→            print(colorize(f"  Cluster {name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   370→            return
   371→
   372→    if item_pattern is not None:
   373→        _reorder_within_cluster(args, plan, clusters, cluster_names, position, target, item_pattern)
   374→    else:
   375→        _reorder_whole_clusters(plan, clusters, cluster_names, position, target)
```
