```
   450→
   451→def _is_synthetic_id(fid: str) -> bool:
   452→    """Return True if the ID is a synthetic workflow/triage item, not a real issue."""
   453→    return fid.startswith("triage::") or fid.startswith("workflow::") or fid.startswith("subjective::")
   454→
   455→
   456→def _resolve_synthetic_ids(patterns: list[str]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
   457→    """Separate synthetic IDs from real issue patterns.
   458→
   459→    Returns (synthetic_ids, remaining_patterns).
   460→    """
   461→    synthetic = [p for p in patterns if _is_synthetic_id(p)]
   462→    remaining = [p for p in patterns if not _is_synthetic_id(p)]
   463→    return synthetic, remaining
   464→
   465→
   466→def _blocked_triage_stages(plan: dict) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
   467→    """Return ``{stage_id: [blocked_by_ids]}`` for triage stages that can't run yet.
   468→
   469→    Uses the dependency graph and confirmed-stage metadata directly —
   470→    no state needed, no queue item construction.
   471→    """
   472→    order_set = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   473→    present = order_set & TRIAGE_IDS
   474→    if not present:
   475→        return {}
   476→
   477→    confirmed = set(plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {}).get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   478→    stage_names = ("observe", "reflect", "organize", "commit")
   479→
   480→    blocked: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
   481→    for sid, name in zip(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS, stage_names, strict=False):
   482→        if sid not in present or name in confirmed:
   483→            continue
   484→        deps = TRIAGE_STAGE_DEPENDENCIES.get(name, set())
   485→        unmet = sorted(
   486→            f"triage::{dep}" for dep in deps
   487→            if f"triage::{dep}" in present and dep not in confirmed
   488→        )
   489→        if unmet:
   490→            blocked[sid] = unmet
   491→    return blocked
   492→
   493→
   494→def cmd_plan_resolve(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   495→    """Mark issues as fixed — delegates to cmd_resolve for rich UX."""
   496→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   497→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attest", None)
   498→    note: str | None = getattr(args, "note", None)
   499→
   500→    # --confirm: auto-generate attestation from --note
   501→    if getattr(args, "confirm", False):
   502→        if not note:
   503→            print(colorize("  --confirm requires --note to describe what you did.", "red"))
   504→            return
   505→        attestation = f"I have actually {note} and I am not gaming the score."
   506→        args.attest = attestation
   507→
   508→    # Handle synthetic IDs (triage::*, workflow::*, subjective::*) directly
   509→    synthetic_ids, real_patterns = _resolve_synthetic_ids(patterns)
   510→    if synthetic_ids:
   511→        plan = load_plan()
   512→        # Validate triage dependency chain
   513→        blocked_map = _blocked_triage_stages(plan)
   514→        for sid in synthetic_ids:
   515→            if sid in blocked_map:
   516→                deps = ", ".join(b.replace("triage::", "") for b in blocked_map[sid])
   517→                print(colorize(f"  Cannot resolve {sid} — blocked by: {deps}", "red"))
   518→                print(colorize("  Complete those stages first, or use --force-resolve to override.", "dim"))
   519→                if not getattr(args, "force_resolve", False):
   520→                    return
   521→
   522→        # Gate workflow items behind triage completion
   523→        GATED_WORKFLOW_IDS = {WORKFLOW_SCORE_CHECKPOINT_ID, WORKFLOW_CREATE_PLAN_ID}
   524→        gated_ids = [sid for sid in synthetic_ids if sid in GATED_WORKFLOW_IDS]
   525→        if gated_ids:
   526→            force = getattr(args, "force_resolve", False)
   527→            meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   528→            # Triage is complete if last_completed_at is set (stages archive on --complete)
   529→            triage_ever_completed = bool(meta.get("last_completed_at"))
   530→            if triage_ever_completed:
   531→                # --complete archives stages and sets last_completed_at → all 4 done
   532→                missing: set[str] = set()
   533→            else:
   534→                confirmed_stages = set(meta.get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   535→                required_stages = {"observe", "reflect", "organize", "commit"}
   536→                missing = required_stages - confirmed_stages
   537→
   538→            if missing and not force:
   539→                # Auto-inject triage stages if not already in queue
   540→                if not has_triage_in_queue(plan):
   541→                    inject_triage_stages(plan)
   542→                    meta.setdefault("triage_stages", {})
   543→                    plan["epic_triage_meta"] = meta
   544→                    save_plan(plan)
   545→
   546→                # Print targeted error based on which stage is next
   547→                stage_order = ["observe", "reflect", "organize", "commit"]
   548→                next_stage = next((s for s in stage_order if s in missing), "observe")
   549→
   550→                for wid in gated_ids:
   551→                    print(colorize(f"  Cannot resolve {wid} — triage not complete.", "red"))
   552→                print()
   553→
   554→                if next_stage == "observe":
   555→                    print(colorize("  You must analyze the findings before resolving this.", "yellow"))
   556→                    print(colorize("  Start by examining themes, root causes, and contradictions:", "dim"))
   557→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --stage observe --report "..."', "dim"))
   558→                    print()
   559→                    print(colorize("  The report must be 100+ chars describing what you found.", "dim"))
   560→                elif next_stage == "reflect":
   561→                    print(colorize("  Observe is done. Now compare against previously completed work:", "yellow"))
   562→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --stage reflect --report "..."', "dim"))
   563→                    print()
   564→                    print(colorize("  The report must mention recurring dimensions if any exist.", "dim"))
   565→                elif next_stage == "organize":
   566→                    print(colorize("  Reflect is done. Now create clusters and prioritize:", "yellow"))
   567→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster create <name> --description "..."', "dim"))
   568→                    print(colorize("    desloppify plan cluster add <name> <issue-patterns>", "dim"))
   569→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --steps "step1" "step2"', "dim"))
   570→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --stage organize --report "..."', "dim"))
   571→                    print()
   572→                    print(colorize("  All manual clusters must have descriptions and action_steps.", "dim"))
   573→                elif next_stage == "commit":
   574→                    print(colorize("  Organize is done. Finalize the execution plan:", "yellow"))
   575→                    print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --complete --strategy "..."', "dim"))
   576→
   577→                print()
   578→                print(colorize(f"  Remaining stages: {', '.join(sorted(missing))}", "dim"))
   579→                print(colorize(
   580→                    "  To skip triage: --force-resolve --note 'reason for skipping triage'",
   581→                    "dim",
   582→                ))
   583→
   584→                # Log the blocked attempt
   585→                append_log_entry(
   586→                    plan, "workflow_blocked",
   587→                    issue_ids=gated_ids, actor="user",
   588→                    note=note,
   589→                    detail={"missing_stages": sorted(missing), "next_stage": next_stage},
   590→                )
   591→                save_plan(plan)
   592→                return
   593→
   594→            if missing and force:
   595→                # Force-resolve: require substantial note, log prominently
   596→                if not note or len(note.strip()) < 50:
   597→                    print(colorize(
   598→                        f"  --force-resolve still requires --note (min 50 chars) explaining "
   599→                        f"why you're skipping triage.",
   600→                        "red",
   601→                    ))
   602→                    return
   603→                print(colorize(
   604→                    "  WARNING: Skipping triage requirement — this is logged.",
   605→                    "yellow",
   606→                ))
   607→                append_log_entry(
   608→                    plan, "workflow_force_skip",
   609→                    issue_ids=gated_ids, actor="user",
   610→                    note=note,
   611→                    detail={"forced": True, "missing_stages": sorted(missing)},
   612→                )
   613→                save_plan(plan)
   614→                # Fall through to scan gate / purge_ids below
   615→
   616→        # Gate workflow items behind scan completion
   617→        if gated_ids:
   618→            scan_count_at_start = plan.get("scan_count_at_plan_start")
   619→            if scan_count_at_start is not None:
   620→                resolved_state_path = state_path(args)
   621→                state_data = state_mod.load_state(resolved_state_path)
   622→                current_scan_count = int(state_data.get("scan_count", 0) or 0)
   623→                scan_ran = current_scan_count > scan_count_at_start
   624→                scan_skipped = plan.get("scan_gate_skipped", False)
   625→
   626→                if not scan_ran and not scan_skipped and not force:
   627→                    for wid in gated_ids:
   628→                        print(colorize(
   629→                            f"  Cannot resolve {wid} — no scan has run this cycle.",
   630→                            "red",
   631→                        ))
   632→                    print()
   633→                    print(colorize(
   634→                        "  You must run a scan before resolving workflow items:",
   635→                        "yellow",
   636→                    ))
   637→                    print(colorize("    desloppify scan", "dim"))
   638→                    print()
   639→                    print(colorize(
   640→                        f"  Scans at cycle start: {scan_count_at_start}  "
   641→                        f"Current: {current_scan_count}",
   642→                        "dim",
   643→                    ))
   644→                    print(colorize(
   645→                        "  To skip scan requirement: desloppify plan scan-gate --skip "
   646→                        '--note "reason for skipping scan"',
   647→                        "dim",
   648→                    ))
   649→                    print(colorize(
   650→                        "  Or use: --force-resolve --note 'reason for skipping'",
   651→                        "dim",
   652→                    ))
   653→
   654→                    append_log_entry(
   655→                        plan, "scan_gate_blocked",
   656→                        issue_ids=gated_ids, actor="user",
   657→                        note=note,
   658→                        detail={
   659→                            "scan_count_at_start": scan_count_at_start,
   660→                            "current_scan_count": current_scan_count,
   661→                        },
   662→                    )
   663→                    save_plan(plan)
   664→                    return
   665→
   666→        purge_ids(plan, synthetic_ids)
   667→        append_log_entry(
   668→            plan, "done", issue_ids=synthetic_ids, actor="user", note=note,
   669→        )
   670→        save_plan(plan)
   671→        for sid in synthetic_ids:
   672→            print(colorize(f"  Resolved: {sid}", "green"))
   673→        if not real_patterns:
   674→            return
   675→        # Continue with remaining real patterns
   676→        patterns = real_patterns
   677→        args.patterns = patterns
   678→
   679→    # Validate note length
   680→    if not validate_note_length(note):
   681→        show_note_length_requirement(note)
   682→        return
   683→
   684→    # Pre-validate attestation before delegating (avoids stale hint in resolve)
   685→    if not validate_attestation(attestation):
   686→        show_attestation_requirement("Plan resolve", attestation, ATTEST_EXAMPLE)
   687→        return
   688→
   689→    # Cluster completion guard: block bulk-completing small clusters
   690→    try:
   691→        runtime = command_runtime(args)
   692→        state = runtime.state
   693→        plan = load_plan()
   694→        if _check_cluster_guard(patterns, plan, state):
   695→            return
   696→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   697→        plan = None
   698→
   699→    # Log the done action (best-effort)
   700→    try:
   701→        if plan is None:
   702→            plan = load_plan()
   703→        clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   704→        cluster_name = None
   705→        for p in patterns:
   706→            if p in clusters:
   707→                cluster_name = p
   708→                break
   709→        append_log_entry(
   710→            plan,
   711→            "done",
   712→            issue_ids=patterns,
   713→            cluster_name=cluster_name,
   714→            actor="user",
   715→            note=note,
   716→        )
   717→        save_plan(plan)
   718→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   719→        log_best_effort_failure(logger, "append plan resolve log entry", exc)
   720→        print(colorize(f"  Note: unable to append plan resolve log entry ({exc}).", "dim"))
   721→
   722→    # Build a Namespace that cmd_resolve expects
   723→    resolve_args = argparse.Namespace(
   724→        status="fixed",
   725→        patterns=patterns,
   726→        note=note,
   727→        attest=attestation,
   728→        confirm_batch_wontfix=False,
   729→        force_resolve=bool(getattr(args, "force_resolve", False)),
   730→        state=getattr(args, "state", None),
   731→        lang=getattr(args, "lang", None),
   732→        path=getattr(args, "path", None),
   733→        exclude=getattr(args, "exclude", None),
   734→    )
   735→
   736→    cmd_resolve(resolve_args)
   737→

   739→def cmd_plan_focus(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:

   747→        clear_focus(plan)

   756→    if not cluster_name:

   758→        if active:

   776→
   777→def cmd_plan_scan_gate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   778→    """Check or skip the scan requirement for workflow items."""
   779→    skip = getattr(args, "skip", False)
   780→    note: str | None = getattr(args, "note", None)
   781→
   782→    plan = load_plan()
   783→    scan_count_at_start = plan.get("scan_count_at_plan_start")
   784→
   785→    if scan_count_at_start is None:
   786→        print(colorize("  No active plan cycle (plan_start_scores not seeded).", "dim"))
   787→        print(colorize("  Scan gate is not applicable — workflow items gate themselves.", "dim"))
   788→        return
   789→
   790→    resolved_state_path = state_path(args)
   791→    state_data = state_mod.load_state(resolved_state_path)
   792→    current_scan_count = int(state_data.get("scan_count", 0) or 0)
   793→    scan_ran = current_scan_count > scan_count_at_start
   794→    scan_skipped = plan.get("scan_gate_skipped", False)
   795→
   796→    if not skip:
   797→        # Status check
   798→        if scan_ran:
   799→            print(colorize("  Scan gate: PASSED", "green"))
   800→            print(colorize(
   801→                f"  Scans at cycle start: {scan_count_at_start}  "
   802→                f"Current: {current_scan_count}",
   803→                "dim",
   804→            ))
   805→        elif scan_skipped:
   806→            print(colorize("  Scan gate: SKIPPED (manually)", "yellow"))
   807→        else:
   808→            print(colorize("  Scan gate: BLOCKED", "red"))
   809→            print(colorize(
   810→                f"  Scans at cycle start: {scan_count_at_start}  "
   811→                f"Current: {current_scan_count}",
   812→                "dim",
   813→            ))
   814→            print(colorize("  Run: desloppify scan", "dim"))
   815→            print(colorize(
   816→                '  Or:  desloppify plan scan-gate --skip --note "reason"',
   817→                "dim",
   818→            ))
   819→        return
   820→
   821→    # --skip mode
   822→    if scan_ran:
   823→        print(colorize("  Scan already ran this cycle — no skip needed.", "green"))
   824→        return
   825→
   826→    if not note or len(note.strip()) < 50:
   827→        print(colorize(
```

```
    81→class WorkQueueResult(TypedDict):

    90→def build_work_queue(
    91→    state: StateModel,
    92→    *,
    93→    options: QueueBuildOptions | None = None,
    94→) -> WorkQueueResult:
    95→    """Build a ranked work queue from state issues.
    96→
    97→    Pipeline:
    98→    1. Gather    — issue items, subjective dimensions, workflow stages
    99→    2. Score     — estimate impact from dimension headroom, apply floor
   100→    3. Presort   — stamp plan positions, separate skipped items
   101→    4. Lifecycle — filter endgame-only items when objective work remains
   102→    5. Sort      — rank by impact/confidence, apply plan order
   103→    6. Limit     — truncate to count, optionally add explain metadata
   104→    """
   105→    opts = options or QueueBuildOptions()
   106→    plan, scan_path, status, threshold = _resolve_inputs(opts, state)
   107→
   108→    # 1. Gather
   109→    items = build_issue_items(
   110→        state, scan_path=scan_path, status_filter=status,
   111→        scope=opts.scope, chronic=opts.chronic,
   112→    )
   113→    items += _gather_subjective_items(state, opts, threshold)
   114→    items += _gather_workflow_items(state, plan, status)
   115→
   116→    # 2. Score & filter
   117→    enrich_with_impact(items, state.get("dimension_scores", {}))
   118→    items = [i for i in items if _passes_impact_floor(i)]
   119→
   120→    # 3. Plan-aware ordering (part 1: separate skipped items)
   121→    new_ids, skipped = _plan_presort(items, state, plan)
   122→
   123→    # 4. Lifecycle filter — endgame-only items filtered when objective work remains
   124→    items = _apply_lifecycle_filter(items)
   125→
   126→    # 5. Sort & plan post-processing
   127→    items.sort(key=item_sort_key)
   128→    _plan_postsort(items, skipped, plan, opts)

   130→    # 6. Finalize

   134→    if opts.count is not None and opts.count > 0:
   135→        items = items[:opts.count]
   136→    if opts.explain:
   137→        for item in items:
   138→            item["explain"] = item_explain(item)
   139→
   140→    return {
   141→        "items": items,
   142→        "total": total,
   143→        "grouped": group_queue_items(items, "item"),
   144→        "new_ids": new_ids,
   145→    }

   152→
   153→def _resolve_inputs(
   154→    opts: QueueBuildOptions, state: StateModel,
   155→) -> tuple[dict | None, str | None, str, float]:
   156→    """Resolve plan, scan_path, status, and subjective threshold from options."""
   157→    ctx = opts.context
   158→    plan = ctx.plan if ctx is not None else opts.plan
   159→
   160→    scan_path: str | None = (
   161→        state.get("scan_path")
   162→        if opts.scan_path is _SCAN_PATH_FROM_STATE
   163→        else opts.scan_path  # type: ignore[assignment]
   164→    )
   165→
   166→    status = opts.status
   167→    if status not in ALL_STATUSES:
   168→        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported status filter: {status}")
   169→
   170→    try:
   171→        threshold = float(opts.subjective_threshold)
   172→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
   173→        threshold = 100.0
   174→    threshold = max(0.0, min(100.0, threshold))
   175→
   176→    return plan, scan_path, status, threshold
   177→
   178→
   179→def _gather_subjective_items(
   180→    state: StateModel,
   181→    opts: QueueBuildOptions,
   182→    threshold: float,
   183→) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   184→    """Build subjective dimension candidates.
   185→
   186→    Lifecycle filtering (endgame gating) happens in _apply_lifecycle_filter,
   187→    not here. This function only handles configuration and scope.
   188→    """
   189→    if not opts.include_subjective:
   190→        return []
   191→    if opts.status not in {"open", "all"}:
   192→        return []
   193→    if opts.chronic:
   194→        return []
   195→
   196→    candidates = build_subjective_items(
   197→        state, state.get("issues", {}), threshold=threshold,
   198→    )
   199→    return [item for item in candidates if scope_matches(item, opts.scope)]
```

```
1→"""Plan persistence — load/save with atomic writes."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import json
     6→import logging
     7→import shutil
     8→import sys
     9→from pathlib import Path
    10→
    11→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import safe_write_text
    12→from desloppify.base.output.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
    13→from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import (
    14→    PLAN_VERSION,
    15→    PlanModel,
    16→    empty_plan,
    17→    ensure_plan_defaults,
    18→    validate_plan,
    19→)
    20→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import STATE_DIR, json_default, utc_now
    21→
    22→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    23→
    24→PLAN_FILE = STATE_DIR / "plan.json"
    25→
    26→
    27→def load_plan(path: Path | None = None) -> PlanModel:
    28→    """Load plan from disk, or return empty plan on missing/corruption."""
    29→    plan_path = path or PLAN_FILE
    30→    if not plan_path.exists():
    31→        return empty_plan()
    32→
    33→    try:
    34→        data = json.loads(plan_path.read_text())
    35→    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError) as ex:
    36→        # Try backup before giving up
    37→        backup = plan_path.with_suffix(".json.bak")
    38→        if backup.exists():
    39→            try:
    40→                data = json.loads(backup.read_text())
    41→                logger.warning("Plan file corrupted (%s), loaded from backup.", ex)
    42→                print(f"  Warning: Plan file corrupted ({ex}), loaded from backup.", file=sys.stderr)
    43→                # Fall through to validation below
    44→            except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError) as backup_ex:
    45→                logger.warning("Plan file and backup both corrupted: %s / %s", ex, backup_ex)
    46→                print(f"  Warning: Plan file corrupted ({ex}). Starting fresh.", file=sys.stderr)
    47→                return empty_plan()
    48→        else:
    49→            logger.warning("Plan file corrupted (%s). Starting fresh.", ex)
    50→            print(f"  Warning: Plan file corrupted ({ex}). Starting fresh.", file=sys.stderr)
    51→            return empty_plan()
    52→
    53→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
    54→        logger.warning("Plan file root is not a JSON object. Starting fresh.")
    55→        print("  Warning: Plan file root must be a JSON object. Starting fresh.", file=sys.stderr)
    56→        return empty_plan()
    57→
    58→    version = data.get("version", 1)
    59→    if version > PLAN_VERSION:
    60→        logger.warning("Plan file version %d > supported %d.", version, PLAN_VERSION)
    61→        print(
    62→            f"  Warning: Plan file version {version} is newer than supported "
    63→            f"({PLAN_VERSION}). Some features may not work correctly.",
    64→            file=sys.stderr,
    65→        )
    66→
    67→    ensure_plan_defaults(data)
    68→    try:
    69→        validate_plan(data)
    70→    except ValueError as ex:
    71→        logger.warning("Plan invariants invalid (%s). Starting fresh.", ex)
    72→        print(f"  Warning: Plan invariants invalid ({ex}). Starting fresh.", file=sys.stderr)
    73→        return empty_plan()
    74→
    75→    return data  # type: ignore[return-value]
    76→
    77→
    78→def save_plan(plan: PlanModel | dict, path: Path | None = None) -> None:
    79→    """Validate and save plan to disk atomically."""
    80→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
    81→    plan["updated"] = utc_now()
    82→    validate_plan(plan)
    83→
    84→    plan_path = path or PLAN_FILE
    85→    plan_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    86→
    87→    content = json.dumps(plan, indent=2, default=json_default) + "\n"
    88→
    89→    if plan_path.exists():
    90→        backup = plan_path.with_suffix(".json.bak")
    91→        try:
    92→            shutil.copy2(str(plan_path), str(backup))
    93→        except OSError as backup_ex:
    94→            log_best_effort_failure(logger, "create plan backup", backup_ex)
    95→
    96→    try:
    97→        safe_write_text(plan_path, content)
    98→    except OSError as ex:
    99→        print(f"  Warning: Could not save plan: {ex}", file=sys.stderr)
   100→        raise
   101→
   102→
   103→def plan_path_for_state(state_path: Path) -> Path:
   104→    """Derive plan.json path from a state file path."""
   105→    return state_path.parent / "plan.json"
   106→
   107→
   108→def has_living_plan(path: Path | None = None) -> bool:
   109→    """Return True if a plan.json exists and has user intent."""
   110→    plan_path = path or PLAN_FILE
   111→    if not plan_path.exists():
   112→        return False
   113→    plan = load_plan(plan_path)
   114→    return bool(
   115→        plan.get("queue_order")
   116→        or plan.get("overrides")
   117→        or plan.get("clusters")
   118→    )
   119→
   120→
   121→__all__ = [
   122→    "PLAN_FILE",
   123→    "has_living_plan",
   124→    "load_plan",
   125→    "plan_path_for_state",
   126→    "save_plan",
   127→]
   128→
```

```
1→"""State-backed work queue for review issues.
     2→
     3→Review issues live in state["issues"]. This module provides:
     4→- Listing/sorting open review issues by impact
     5→- Storing investigation notes on issues
     6→- Expiring stale holistic issues during scan
     7→"""
     8→
     9→from __future__ import annotations
    10→
    11→import logging
    12→from datetime import UTC, datetime
    13→
    14→from desloppify.base.output.issues import issue_weight
    15→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.helpers import detail_dict
    16→
    17→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    18→
    19→__all__ = [
    20→    "impact_label",
    21→    "list_open_review_issues",
    22→    "update_investigation",
    23→    "expire_stale_holistic",
    24→]
    25→
    26→
    27→def impact_label(weight: float) -> str:
    28→    """Convert weight to a human-readable impact label."""
    29→    try:
    30→        numeric = float(weight)
    31→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    32→        return "+"
    33→    if numeric >= 8:
    34→        return "+++"
    35→    if numeric >= 5:
    36→        return "++"
    37→    return "+"
    38→
    39→
    40→def list_open_review_issues(state: dict) -> list[dict]:
    41→    """Return open review issues sorted by impact (highest first)."""
    42→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
    43→    review = [
    44→        issue
    45→        for issue in issues.values()
    46→        if issue.get("status") == "open" and issue.get("detector") == "review"
    47→    ]
    48→
    49→    def _sort_key(issue: dict) -> tuple[float, str]:
    50→        weight, _impact, issue_id = issue_weight(issue)
    51→        return (-weight, issue_id)
    52→
    53→    review.sort(key=_sort_key)
    54→    return review
    55→
    56→
    57→def update_investigation(state: dict, issue_id: str, text: str) -> bool:
    58→    """Store investigation text on a issue. Returns False if not found/not open."""
    59→    issue = state.get("issues", {}).get(issue_id)
    60→    if not issue or issue.get("status") != "open":
    61→        return False
    62→    detail = detail_dict(issue)
    63→    if not detail:
    64→        detail = {}
    65→        issue["detail"] = detail
    66→    detail["investigation"] = text
    67→    detail["investigated_at"] = datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()
    68→    return True
    69→
    70→
    71→def expire_stale_holistic(state: dict, max_age_days: int = 30) -> list[str]:
    72→    """Auto-resolve holistic review issues older than max_age_days."""
    73→    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    74→    expired: list[str] = []
    75→
    76→    for issue_id, issue in state.get("issues", {}).items():
    77→        if issue.get("detector") != "review":
    78→            continue
    79→        if issue.get("status") != "open":
    80→            continue
    81→        if not detail_dict(issue).get("holistic"):
    82→            continue
    83→
    84→        last_seen = issue.get("last_seen")
    85→        if not last_seen:
    86→            continue
    87→
    88→        try:
    89→            seen_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(last_seen)
    90→        except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
    91→            logger.debug(
    92→                "Skipping holistic issue %s with invalid last_seen %r: %s",
    93→                issue_id,
    94→                last_seen,
    95→                exc,
    96→            )
    97→            continue
    98→
    99→        age_days = (now - seen_dt).days
   100→        if age_days > max_age_days:
   101→            issue["status"] = "auto_resolved"
   102→            issue["resolved_at"] = now.isoformat()
   103→            issue["note"] = "holistic review expired — re-run review to re-evaluate"
   104→            expired.append(issue_id)
   105→
   106→    return expired
   107→
```

```
def is_holistic_subjective_issue(issue: dict, *, issue_id: str = "") -> bool:
    """Best-effort check for holistic subjective-review coverage issues."""
    candidate_id = str(issue.get("id") or issue_id or "")
    if "::holistic_unreviewed" in candidate_id or "::holistic_stale" in candidate_id:
        return True

    summary = str(issue.get("summary", "") or "").lower()
    if "holistic" in summary and "review" in summary:
        return True

    detail = issue.get("detail", {})
    return bool(detail.get("holistic"))
```

```
    17→def new_item_ids(state: StateModel) -> set[str]:
    18→    """Return issue IDs added in the most recent scan."""
    19→    scan_history = state.get("scan_history", [])
    20→    if not scan_history:
    21→        return set()
    22→    threshold = scan_history[-1].get("timestamp", "")
    23→    if not threshold:
    24→        return set()
    25→    return {
    26→        issue_id
    27→        for issue_id, issue in state.get("issues", {}).items()
    28→        if issue.get("first_seen", "") >= threshold
    29→    }

    32→def enrich_plan_metadata(items: list[WorkQueueItem], plan: dict) -> None:
    33→    """Stamp plan description, note, and cluster info from overrides."""
    34→    clusters: dict = plan.get("clusters", {})
    35→
    36→    for item in items:
    37→        issue_id = item["id"]
    38→        description = get_issue_description(plan, issue_id)
    39→        note = get_issue_note(plan, issue_id)
    40→        override = get_issue_override(plan, issue_id)
    41→        if description:
    42→            item["plan_description"] = description
    43→        if note:
    44→            item["plan_note"] = note
    45→        if override.get("cluster"):
    46→            cluster_name = override["cluster"]
    47→            cluster_data = clusters.get(cluster_name, {})
    48→            item["plan_cluster"] = {
    49→                "name": cluster_name,
    50→                "description": cluster_data.get("description"),
    51→                "total_items": len(cluster_data.get("issue_ids", [])),
    52→                "action_steps": cluster_data.get("action_steps") or [],
    53→            }

    56→def stamp_plan_sort_keys(
    57→    items: list[WorkQueueItem],
    58→    plan: dict,
    59→    new_ids: set[str],
    60→) -> None:
    61→    """Stamp ``_plan_position`` and ``_is_new`` on each item.
    62→
    63→    These fields are consumed by :func:`item_sort_key` in ``ranking.py``
    64→    to produce the correct final ordering in a single sort pass.
    65→    """
    66→    queue_order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
    67→    skipped_ids: set[str] = set(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
    68→
    69→    position_map: dict[str, int] = {}
    70→    for idx, issue_id in enumerate(queue_order):
    71→        if issue_id not in skipped_ids:
    72→            position_map[issue_id] = idx
    73→
    74→    for item in items:
    75→        item_id = item["id"]
    76→        pos = position_map.get(item_id)
    77→        item["_plan_position"] = pos  # None if not in queue_order
    78→        item["_is_new"] = item_id in new_ids
    79→
    80→
    81→def separate_skipped(
    82→    items: list[WorkQueueItem],
    83→    plan: dict,
    84→) -> tuple[list[WorkQueueItem], list[WorkQueueItem]]:
    85→    """Separate skipped items from the main list.
    86→
    87→    Returns ``(non_skipped, skipped)`` so callers can optionally re-append.
    88→    """
    89→    skipped_ids: set[str] = set(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
    90→    if not skipped_ids:
    91→        return items, []
    92→    non_skipped: list[WorkQueueItem] = []
    93→    skipped: list[WorkQueueItem] = []
    94→    for item in items:
    95→        if item["id"] in skipped_ids:
    96→            skipped.append(item)
    97→        else:
    98→            non_skipped.append(item)
    99→    return non_skipped, skipped

   102→def filter_cluster_focus(
   103→    items: list[WorkQueueItem],
   104→    plan: dict,
   105→    cluster: str | None,
   106→) -> list[WorkQueueItem]:
   107→    """Filter to only cluster members when a cluster focus is active."""
   108→    effective_cluster = cluster or plan.get("active_cluster")
   109→    if not effective_cluster:
   110→        return items
   111→    clusters: dict = plan.get("clusters", {})
   112→    cluster_data = clusters.get(effective_cluster, {})
   113→    cluster_member_ids = set(cluster_data.get("issue_ids", []))
   114→    if not cluster_member_ids:
   115→        return items
   116→    return [item for item in items if item["id"] in cluster_member_ids]

   119→def stamp_positions(items: list[WorkQueueItem], plan: dict) -> None:
   120→    """Stamp queue_position and plan_skipped metadata on each item."""
   121→    skipped_map: dict = plan.get("skipped", {})
   122→    skipped_ids: set[str] = set(skipped_map.keys())
   123→
   124→    for position, item in enumerate(items):
   125→        item["queue_position"] = position + 1
   126→        if item["id"] in skipped_ids:
   127→            item["plan_skipped"] = True
   128→            skip_entry = skipped_map.get(item["id"])
   129→            if skip_entry:
   130→                item["plan_skip_kind"] = skip_entry.get("kind", "temporary")
   131→                skip_reason = skip_entry.get("reason")
   132→                if skip_reason:
   133→                    item["plan_skip_reason"] = skip_reason

   136→def action_type_for_detector(detector: str) -> str:
   137→    """Look up the action_type for a detector from the registry."""
   138→    meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   139→    if meta:
   140→        return meta.action_type
   141→    return "manual_fix"
   142→
   143→
   144→def _build_cluster_meta(
   145→    cluster_name: str, members: list[WorkQueueItem], cluster_data: dict[str, Any]
   146→) -> WorkQueueItem:
   147→    """Build a cluster meta-item from its member items."""
   148→    detector = members[0].get("detector", "") if members else ""
   149→    action = cluster_data.get("action") or ""
   150→    if "desloppify autofix" in action:
   151→        action_type = "auto_fix"
   152→    elif "desloppify move" in action:
   153→        action_type = "reorganize"
   154→    else:
   155→        action_type = action_type_for_detector(detector)
   156→        if action_type == "auto_fix" and "desloppify autofix" not in action:
   157→            action_type = "refactor"
   158→
   159→    stored_desc = cluster_data.get("description") or ""
   160→    total_in_cluster = len(cluster_data.get("issue_ids", []))
   161→    if stored_desc and total_in_cluster != len(members):
   162→        summary = stored_desc.replace(str(total_in_cluster), str(len(members)))
   163→    else:
   164→        summary = stored_desc or f"{len(members)} issues"
   165→
   166→    primary_command = cluster_data.get("action")
   167→    if not primary_command:
   168→        primary_command = f"desloppify next --cluster {cluster_name} --count 10"
   169→
   170→    estimated_impact = max(
   171→        (m.get("estimated_impact", 0.0) for m in members), default=0.0
   172→    )
   173→
   174→    return {
   175→        "id": cluster_name,
   176→        "kind": "cluster",
   177→        "action_type": action_type,
   178→        "summary": summary,
   179→        "members": members,
   180→        "member_count": len(members),
   181→        "primary_command": primary_command,
   182→        "cluster_name": cluster_name,
   183→        "cluster_auto": True,

   186→        "detector": detector,
   187→        "file": "",
   188→        "estimated_impact": estimated_impact,
   189→        "action_steps": cluster_data.get("action_steps") or [],
   190→    }
```

## Summary of Findings: Desloppify Cluster Step Storage & Display

Based on thorough analysis of the desloppify codebase, here's the complete picture:

### 1. **How steps are stored in plan.json**

**File**: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/schema.py` (lines 42-63)

The Cluster TypedDict defines:
```python
class Cluster(TypedDict, total=False):
    name: Required[str]
    description: str | None
    issue_ids: list[str]
    created_at: str
    updated_at: str
    auto: bool
    cluster_key: str
    action: str | None
    user_modified: bool
    action_steps: list[str]  # <-- Steps stored here
    source_clusters: list[str]
    status: str
    # ... other fields
```

**In plan.json structure** (confirmed from `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/.desloppify/plan.json` lines 16-33):
```json

  "fix-naming": {

      "step 1",
      "step 2"
    ],
    "auto": false,
    "user_modified": true,
    "created_at": "2025-06-01T00:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2025-06-01T00:00:00Z",

  }

```

### 2. **How `cluster update --steps` works**

**File**: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/cluster_handlers.py` (lines 522-558)

The `_cmd_cluster_update` function:
- Line 526: Gets `steps: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "steps", None)`
- Lines 540-541: Directly assigns to cluster: `cluster["action_steps"] = list(steps)`
- Lines 542-549: Prints stored steps with cleanup (removes leading numbers like "1. ")
- Line 550: Sets `cluster["user_modified"] = True`
- Line 551: Sets `cluster["updated_at"] = utc_now()`
- Lines 552-557: Appends log entry and saves plan

### 3. **How `cluster show` renders**

**File**: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/cluster_handlers.py` (lines 399-441)

The `_cmd_cluster_show` function:
- Lines 419-423: Displays action_steps if present:
```python
steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
if steps:
    print(colorize(f"  Steps ({len(steps)}):", "dim"))
    for i, step in enumerate(steps, 1):
        print(colorize(f"    {i}. {step}", "dim"))
```

### 5. **The `--steps` CLI argument definition**

**File**: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/cli_support/parser_groups_plan_impl.py` (lines 225-229)

```python
# plan cluster update <name> [--description "..."] [--steps "..." ...]
p_cu = cluster_sub.add_parser("update", help="Update cluster description and/or action steps")
p_cu.add_argument("cluster_name", type=str, help="Cluster name")
p_cu.add_argument("--description", type=str, default=None, help="Cluster description")
p_cu.add_argument("--steps", nargs="+", metavar="STEP", default=None, help="Action steps list")
```

Key details:
- **`nargs="+"`** - requires at least 1 step; multiple steps can be passed
- **Multiple invocations**: Each `--steps "step text"` becomes one item in the list
- Example: `desloppify plan cluster update my-cluster --steps "step 1" "step 2" "step 3"`

### 6. **Reorder functionality**

**File**: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/reorder_handlers.py`

The `plan reorder` command (lines 32-73) reorders **issues in the queue**, not clusters themselves.

**Within-cluster reordering**: Available via `plan cluster reorder` (lines 356-376 in cluster_handlers.py):
```python
def _cmd_cluster_reorder(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    # Reorder entire clusters as blocks OR
    # Reorder items within a single cluster using --item pattern
```

Positions supported: `"top", "bottom", "before", "after", "up", "down"`
- `top` / `bottom`: Move to edges
- `before <target>` / `after <target>`: Position relative to another issue
- `up <offset>` / `down <offset>`: Shift by N positions

```python
class Cluster(TypedDict, total=False):

    action: str | None                     # Primary command/guidance
    user_modified: bool                    # Manually edited?
    action_steps: list[str]                # Step list (your focus)

    # ... others: optional, thesis, direction, root_cause, etc.
```

```python
class PlanModel(TypedDict, total=False):

    created: Required[str]

    clusters: dict[str, Cluster]           # All clusters
    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry]          # Skipped issues
    overrides: dict[str, ItemOverride]     # Per-issue annotations
    execution_log: list[ExecutionLogEntry] # Audit trail

```

```python
cmd_plan_describe(args):
  patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
  text: str = getattr(args, "text", "")
  plan = load_plan()
  issue_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, patterns, plan=plan)
  for fid in issue_ids:
    describe_issue(plan, fid, text or None)  # stores in plan.overrides[fid].description
  append_log_entry(plan, "describe", issue_ids=issue_ids, detail={"text": text})
  save_plan(plan)
```

**What it does**:
- Sets arbitrary metadata (text) on issues via the plan override layer

- Already batch-enabled (accepts multiple patterns)

### 6. **Action Steps vs. Issues**
**File**: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/schema.py` lines 42–63 (Cluster type)

**Relationship**:
- `action_steps` is a **separate list** on the cluster itself (line 60)
- `issue_ids` is the list of member issues (line 45)
- Action steps describe **how to resolve** the members, not which issues
- Example: cluster has 15 Python lint issues; `action_steps` might be:
  1. "Run autofix on src/"
  2. "Manually review false positives"
  3. "Test coverage for updated code"

**Steps in output**:
- Shown in `desloppify next` (render.py lines 110–114): appears under cluster card
- Shown in `plan queue --cluster` (render.py lines 363–368): full plan display
- Can be set/updated via `cluster update --steps "s1" "s2" ...` (cluster_handlers.py line 541)

- No built-in mechanism; steps are free text
- Could extend: add a `step_refs: list[str]` field to action_steps if parsing step strings

**Current state**: No explicit priority field on clusters or queue items.

**Ordering mechanism**:
- **Clusters**: sorted by earliest member's position in `queue_order` (plan_order.py lines 443–459)
- **Queue items**: ranked by `item_sort_key()` (ranking.py):
  - Primary: plan position (if in `plan.queue_order`)
  - Secondary: impact estimate (dimension headroom)
  - Tertiary: confidence + detector type
  - Final: issue ID (stable tiebreaker)

- Item sort key (ranking.py): check `item.get("cluster", {}).get("priority")` before impact

I need to design improvements to the desloppify CLI tool's cluster/steps system based on real usage feedback. Here's the context:

## Current State

**Steps storage**: `action_steps: list[str]` on each cluster in plan.json. Steps are flat strings.

**Steps input**: `desloppify plan cluster update <name> --steps "step 1 long text" "step 2 long text"` via `nargs="+"`. Very painful for long multi-sentence steps with special chars.

**Steps display**: `cluster show` shows steps as numbered list (dim color). `cluster list -v` shows step count.

**Schema** (in schema.py):
```python
class Cluster(TypedDict, total=False):
    name: Required[str]
    description: str | None
    issue_ids: list[str]
    action_steps: list[str]  # flat strings
    auto: bool
    user_modified: bool
    priority: ...  # doesn't exist yet
    # ...
```

**Key files**:
- Schema: `desloppify/engine/_plan/schema.py` lines 42-63
- CLI parser: `desloppify/app/cli_support/parser_groups_plan_impl.py` lines 225-229
- Cluster handlers: `desloppify/app/commands/plan/cluster_handlers.py` (update at 522-558, show at 399-441, list at 462-520)
- Queue render: `desloppify/app/commands/plan/queue_render.py`
- Reorder: `desloppify/app/commands/plan/reorder_handlers.py` and cluster_handlers.py lines 356-376

## Problems (from real usage building 16 clusters with 95 total steps)

1. **Steps input is brutal**: Shell escaping for multi-sentence strings. Can't add detail beyond a single line. No way to write steps in a file and submit. Need structured steps with title + detail.

2. **Steps are flat strings**: Need structure — each step should have a title (short summary) and detail (long, can be paragraphs). Currently everything crammed into one string.

3. **`cluster show` doesn't show enough**: Steps are shown but dimmed. Issues don't show file paths or suggestions (have to use `next --cluster` separately). Want a unified view.

4. **Steps vs issues relationship unclear**: Steps describe HOW to fix, issues describe WHAT's wrong. User wants a "meta list" — unified view showing steps alongside the issues they address.

5. **No bulk operations**: Creating 16 clusters + adding steps = 32+ commands. Need batch creation/update from a file.

6. **Organize confirm is two-step**: `triage --stage organize --report "..."` then `triage --confirm organize --attestation "..."`. Confusing.

7. **No priority field**: Priority encoded in descriptions ("PRIORITY 1 — SECURITY"). Need first-class `priority: int` on clusters.

8. **No `--steps` append**: Every `cluster update --steps` replaces ALL steps. Need append/update-by-index.

9. **No diff/preview after update**: "Stored 4 action step(s)" but can't verify what changed.

## User's Vision

The user wants:
- **File-based step authoring**: Write a text document with numbered steps (title + detail), submit it, system parses and stores structured.
- **Unified meta-list**: Steps and issues shown together as one project plan. Steps reference specific issues.
- **Bulk import**: Single file creates/updates multiple clusters.
- **Priority as first-class field**: Native ordering by priority.

## Design Requirements

1. Steps need structured storage: `{title: str, detail: str, issue_refs?: list[str]}`
2. File format for authoring steps — something natural that agents or humans can write
3. Backward compat with existing `list[str]` steps (migration)
4. `cluster show` improvements
5. Batch/bulk operations
6. Priority field
7. Steps append/update operations
8. Simplify organize confirm

Please design a concrete implementation plan with:
- Data model changes (schema.py)
- File format design for step authoring
- CLI changes (new args, new commands)
- Display changes
- Migration path for existing flat steps
- Which changes are highest priority and can be done incrementally

Keep it practical — this is a CLI tool used by AI agents primarily.

```
   163→    completed_clusters: NotRequired[list[dict[str, Any]]]  # legacy snapshot key

   166→def empty_plan() -> PlanModel:
   167→    """Return a new empty plan payload."""
   168→    now = utc_now()
   169→    return {
   170→        "version": PLAN_VERSION,
   171→        "created": now,
   172→        "updated": now,
   173→        "queue_order": [],
   174→        "deferred": [],
   175→        "skipped": {},
   176→        "active_cluster": None,
   177→        "overrides": {},
   178→        "clusters": {},
   179→        "superseded": {},
   180→        "promoted_ids": [],
   181→        "plan_start_scores": {},

   184→        "commit_log": [],
   185→        "uncommitted_issues": [],
   186→        "commit_tracking_branch": None,
   187→    }
   188→
   189→
   190→def ensure_plan_defaults(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   191→    """Normalize a loaded plan to ensure all keys exist.
   192→
   193→    Runtime contract is v7-only. Legacy payloads are upgraded in-place once.
   194→    """
   195→    defaults = empty_plan()
   196→    for key, value in defaults.items():
   197→        plan.setdefault(key, value)
   198→    _upgrade_plan_to_v7(plan)
   199→
   200→
   201→def triage_clusters(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Cluster]:
   202→    """Return clusters whose name starts with ``EPIC_PREFIX``."""
   203→    return {
   204→        name: cluster
   205→        for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items()
   206→        if name.startswith(EPIC_PREFIX)
   207→    }
   208→
   209→
   210→def validate_plan(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   211→    """Raise ValueError when plan invariants are violated."""
   212→    if not isinstance(plan.get("version"), int):
   213→        raise ValueError("plan.version must be an int")
   214→    if not isinstance(plan.get("queue_order"), list):
   215→        raise ValueError("plan.queue_order must be a list")
   216→
   217→    # No ID should appear in both queue_order and skipped
   218→    skipped_ids = set(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
   219→    overlap = set(plan["queue_order"]) & skipped_ids
   220→    if overlap:
   221→        raise ValueError(
   222→            f"IDs cannot appear in both queue_order and skipped: {sorted(overlap)}"
   223→        )
   224→
   225→    # Validate skip entry kinds
   226→    for fid, entry in plan.get("skipped", {}).items():
   227→        kind = entry.get("kind")
   228→        if kind not in VALID_SKIP_KINDS:
   229→            raise ValueError(
   230→                f"Invalid skip kind {kind!r} for {fid}; must be one of {sorted(VALID_SKIP_KINDS)}"
   231→            )
   232→
```

```
    30→def _suggest_close_matches(state: dict, plan: dict | None, patterns: list[str]) -> None:
    31→    """Print fuzzy match suggestions for patterns that resolved to zero issues."""
    32→    all_ids: list[str] = list(state.get("issues", {}).keys())
    33→    if plan is not None:
    34→        seen_ids: set[str] = set(all_ids)
    35→        for fid in plan.get("queue_order", []):
    36→            if fid not in seen_ids:
    37→                seen_ids.add(fid)
    38→                all_ids.append(fid)
    39→        for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
    40→            for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", []):
    41→                if fid not in seen_ids:
    42→                    seen_ids.add(fid)
    43→                    all_ids.append(fid)
    44→
    45→    for pattern in patterns:
    46→        segments = pattern.split("::")
    47→        last_seg = segments[-1]
    48→        suggestions: list[str] = []
    49→
    50→        if _HEX8_RE.match(last_seg):
    51→            suggestions = [fid for fid in all_ids if fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}") or fid == last_seg]
    52→            if suggestions:
    53→                print(colorize(f"  No match for: {pattern!r}", "yellow"))
    54→                print(colorize("  Did you mean:", "dim"))
    55→                for m in suggestions[:3]:
    56→                    print(colorize(f"    {m}", "dim"))
    57→                print(colorize(f"  Tip: match by hash suffix alone: {last_seg}", "dim"))
    58→            continue
    59→
    60→        # Try last segment and second-to-last as descriptive name slugs
    61→        slug = segments[-2] if len(segments) >= 2 else ""
    62→        for fid in all_ids:
    63→            if f"::{last_seg}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}"):
    64→                suggestions.append(fid)
    65→            elif slug and (f"::{slug}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{slug}")):
    66→                suggestions.append(fid)
    67→        if suggestions:
    68→            print(colorize(f"  No match for: {pattern!r}", "yellow"))
    69→            print(colorize("  Did you mean:", "dim"))
    70→            for m in suggestions[:3]:
    71→                print(colorize(f"    {m}", "dim"))
    72→

   210→def _resolve_item_position(
   211→    position: str,
   212→    target: str | None,
   213→    item_ids: list[str],
   214→    ordered_slice: list[str],
   215→    cluster_member_set: set[str],
   216→    cluster_name: str,
   217→    state: dict,
   218→    plan: dict,
   219→) -> tuple[str, str | None, int | None] | None:
   220→    """Resolve where items should be positioned within a cluster.
   221→
   222→    Returns (resolved_position, resolved_target, offset) on success,
   223→    or None if an error was printed and the caller should abort.
   224→    """
   225→    item_set = set(item_ids)
   226→
   227→    if position == "top":
   228→        first_non_item = next((fid for fid in ordered_slice if fid not in item_set), None)
   229→        if first_non_item is None or set(ordered_slice[:len(item_ids)]) == item_set:
   230→            print(colorize("  Already at the top of the cluster.", "yellow"))
   231→            return None
   232→        return ("before", first_non_item, None)
   233→
   234→    if position == "bottom":
   235→        last_non_item = next((fid for fid in reversed(ordered_slice) if fid not in item_set), None)
   236→        if last_non_item is None or set(ordered_slice[-len(item_ids):]) == item_set:
   237→            print(colorize("  Already at the bottom of the cluster.", "yellow"))
   238→            return None
   239→        return ("after", last_non_item, None)
   240→
   241→    if position in ("before", "after"):
   242→        if target is None:
   243→            print(colorize(f"  '{position}' requires a target. Example: --item PAT {position} TARGET", "red"))
   244→            return None
   245→        target_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, [target], plan=plan)
   246→        if not target_ids:
   247→            print(colorize(f"  No match for target {target!r}.", "yellow"))
   248→            return None
   249→        resolved_target = target_ids[0]
   250→        if resolved_target not in cluster_member_set:
   251→            print(colorize(f"  Target {resolved_target!r} is not in cluster {cluster_name!r}.", "red"))
   252→            return None
   253→        return (position, resolved_target, None)
   254→
   255→    if position in ("up", "down"):
   256→        if target is None:
   257→            print(colorize(f"  '{position}' requires an offset. Example: --item PAT {position} 3", "red"))
   258→            return None
   259→        try:
   260→            offset = int(target)
   261→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   262→            print(colorize(f"  Invalid offset: {target}", "red"))
   263→            return None
   264→        return (position, None, offset)
   265→
   266→    return (position, None, None)
   267→
   268→
   269→def _reorder_within_cluster(
   270→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   271→    plan: dict,
   272→    clusters: dict,
   273→    cluster_names: list[str],
   274→    position: str,
   275→    target: str | None,
   276→    item_pattern: str,
   277→) -> None:
   278→    """Reorder items within a single cluster."""
   279→    if len(cluster_names) != 1:
   280→        print(colorize("  --item requires exactly one cluster name.", "red"))
   281→        return
   282→    cluster_name = cluster_names[0]
   283→    cluster_member_set = set(clusters[cluster_name].get("issue_ids", []))
   284→
   285→    state = command_runtime(args).state
   286→    item_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, [item_pattern], plan=plan)
   287→    if not item_ids:
   288→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found for --item pattern.", "yellow"))
   289→        return
   290→    for fid in item_ids:
   291→        if fid not in cluster_member_set:
   292→            print(colorize(f"  {fid!r} is not a member of cluster {cluster_name!r}.", "red"))
   293→            return
   294→
   295→    queue_order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   296→    ordered_slice = [fid for fid in queue_order if fid in cluster_member_set]
   297→
   298→    result = _resolve_item_position(
   299→        position, target, item_ids, ordered_slice,
   300→        cluster_member_set, cluster_name, state, plan,
   301→    )
   302→    if result is None:
   303→        return
   304→    resolved_position, resolved_target, offset = result
   305→
   306→    count = move_items(plan, item_ids, resolved_position, target=resolved_target, offset=offset)
   307→    append_log_entry(
   308→        plan, "cluster_reorder", cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   309→        detail={"position": resolved_position, "count": count, "item": item_pattern},
   310→    )
   311→    save_plan(plan)
   312→    print(colorize(f"  Moved {count} item(s) to {resolved_position} within cluster {cluster_name}.", "green"))
   313→
   314→
   315→def _reorder_whole_clusters(
   316→    plan: dict,
   317→    clusters: dict,
   318→    cluster_names: list[str],
   319→    position: str,
   320→    target: str | None,
   321→) -> None:
   322→    """Reorder entire clusters as blocks relative to each other."""
   323→    target = resolve_target(plan, target, position)
   324→
   325→    offset = None
   326→    if position in ("up", "down") and target is not None:
   327→        try:
   328→            offset = int(target)
   329→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   330→            print(colorize(f"  Invalid offset: {target}", "red"))
   331→            return
   332→        target = None
   333→
   334→    seen: set[str] = set()
   335→    all_member_ids: list[str] = []
   336→    for name in cluster_names:
   337→        for fid in clusters[name].get("issue_ids", []):
   338→            if fid not in seen:
   339→                seen.add(fid)
   340→                all_member_ids.append(fid)
   341→
   342→    if not all_member_ids:
   343→        print(colorize("  No members in the specified cluster(s).", "yellow"))
   344→        return
   345→
   346→    count = move_items(plan, all_member_ids, position, target=target, offset=offset)
   347→    append_log_entry(
   348→        plan, "cluster_reorder", cluster_name=",".join(cluster_names), actor="user",
   349→        detail={"position": position, "count": count},
   350→    )
   351→    save_plan(plan)
   352→    label = ", ".join(cluster_names)
   353→    print(colorize(f"  Moved cluster(s) {label} ({count} items) to {position}.", "green"))
   354→
   355→
   356→def _cmd_cluster_reorder(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   357→    raw_names: str = getattr(args, "cluster_names", "") or getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   358→    cluster_names: list[str] = [n.strip() for n in raw_names.split(",") if n.strip()]
   359→    position: str = getattr(args, "position", "top")
   360→    target: str | None = getattr(args, "target", None)
   361→    item_pattern: str | None = getattr(args, "item_pattern", None)
   362→
   363→    plan = load_plan()
   364→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   365→
   366→    # Validate all names exist
   367→    for name in cluster_names:
   368→        if name not in clusters:
   369→            print(colorize(f"  Cluster {name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   370→            return
   371→
   372→    if item_pattern is not None:
   373→        _reorder_within_cluster(args, plan, clusters, cluster_names, position, target, item_pattern)
   374→    else:
   375→        _reorder_whole_clusters(plan, clusters, cluster_names, position, target)

   378→def _print_cluster_member(idx: int, fid: str, issue: dict | None) -> None:
   379→    """Print a single cluster member line with optional issue details."""
   380→    print(f"    {idx}. {fid}")
   381→    if not issue:
   382→        return
   383→    file = issue.get("file", "")
   384→    lines = issue.get("detail", {}).get("lines", [])
   385→    line_str = f" at lines: {', '.join(str(ln) for ln in lines)}" if lines else ""
   386→    if file:
   387→        print(colorize(f"       File: {file}{line_str}", "dim"))
   388→    summary = issue.get("summary", "")
   389→    if summary:
   390→        print(colorize(f"       {summary}", "dim"))
   391→
   392→
   393→def _load_issues_best_effort(args: argparse.Namespace) -> dict:
   394→    """Load issues from state, returning empty dict on failure."""
   395→    rt = command_runtime(args)
   396→    return rt.state.get("issues", {})
   397→
   398→
   399→def _cmd_cluster_show(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   400→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   401→    plan = load_plan()
   402→    cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(cluster_name)
   403→    if cluster is None:
   404→        print(colorize(f"  Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   405→        return
   406→
   407→    # Header
   408→    auto_tag = "Auto-generated" if cluster.get("auto") else "Manual"
   409→    cluster_key = cluster.get("cluster_key", "")
   410→    key_type = f" ({cluster_key.split('::', 1)[0]})" if cluster_key else ""
   411→    print(colorize(f"  Cluster: {cluster_name}", "bold"))
   412→    print(colorize(f"  Type: {auto_tag}{key_type}", "dim"))
   413→    desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
   414→    if desc:
   415→        print(colorize(f"  Description: {desc}", "dim"))
   416→    action = cluster.get("action") or ""
   417→    if action:
   418→        print(colorize(f"  Action: {action}", "dim"))
   419→    steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   420→    if steps:
   421→        print(colorize(f"  Steps ({len(steps)}):", "dim"))
   422→        for i, step in enumerate(steps, 1):
   423→            print(colorize(f"    {i}. {step}", "dim"))
   424→
   425→    # Members

   427→    if not issue_ids:
   428→        print(colorize("  Members: (none)", "dim"))
   429→    else:
   430→        issues = _load_issues_best_effort(args)
   431→        print(colorize(f"  Members ({len(issue_ids)}):", "dim"))
   432→        for idx, fid in enumerate(issue_ids, 1):
   433→            _print_cluster_member(idx, fid, issues.get(fid))
   434→
   435→    # Commands
   436→    print()
   437→    print(colorize("  Commands:", "dim"))
   438→    print(colorize(f'    Resolve all:  desloppify plan resolve "{cluster_name}" --note "<what>" --attest "..."', "dim"))
   439→    print(colorize(f"    Drill in:     desloppify next --cluster {cluster_name} --count 10", "dim"))
   440→    print(colorize(f"    Skip:         desloppify plan skip {cluster_name}", "dim"))
   441→
   442→
   443→def _sorted_clusters_by_queue_pos(
   444→    clusters: dict, queue_order: list[str],
   445→) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, dict]], dict[str, int]]:
   446→    """Sort clusters by their earliest member's position in the queue.
   447→
   448→    Returns (sorted_cluster_pairs, min_pos_cache) where min_pos_cache maps
   449→    cluster name to its earliest queue position (999_999 if no members queued).
   450→    """
   451→    pos_map = {fid: i for i, fid in enumerate(queue_order)}
   452→
   453→    def _min_pos(cluster_data: dict) -> int:
   454→        positions = [pos_map[fid] for fid in cluster_data.get("issue_ids", []) if fid in pos_map]
   455→        return min(positions) if positions else 999_999
   456→
   457→    min_pos_cache = {name: _min_pos(c) for name, c in clusters.items()}
   458→    sorted_clusters = sorted(clusters.items(), key=lambda kv: min_pos_cache[kv[0]])
   459→    return sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache
   460→
   461→
   462→def _print_cluster_list_verbose(
   463→    sorted_clusters: list[tuple[str, dict]],
   464→    min_pos_cache: dict[str, int],
   465→    active: str | None,
   466→) -> None:
   467→    """Print the verbose table view of the cluster list."""
   468→    name_width = max(20, min(35, max(len(n) for n, _ in sorted_clusters)))
   469→    total = len(sorted_clusters)
   470→    print(colorize(f"  Clusters ({total} total, sorted by queue position):", "bold"))
   471→    print()
   472→    header = f"  {'#pos':<5}  {'Name':<{name_width}}  {'Items':>5}  {'Steps':>5}  {'Type':<6}  Description"
   473→    sep = f"  {'─'*4}  {'─'*name_width}  {'─'*5}  {'─'*5}  {'─'*6}  {'─'*45}"
   474→    print(colorize(header, "dim"))
   475→    print(colorize(sep, "dim"))
   476→    for name, cluster in sorted_clusters:
   477→        min_p = min_pos_cache[name]
   478→        pos_str = f"#{min_p}" if min_p < 999_999 else "—"
   479→        member_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   480→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   481→        steps_str = str(len(steps)) if steps else "—"
   482→        type_str = "auto" if cluster.get("auto") else "manual"
   483→        desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
   484→        if not desc and min_p == 999_999 and not member_count:
   485→            desc = "(no queue position — no members)"
   486→        desc_truncated = (desc[:44] + "…") if len(desc) > 45 else desc
   487→        name_display = (name[:name_width - 1] + "…") if len(name) > name_width else name
   488→        focused = " *" if name == active else ""
   489→        print(f"  {pos_str:>5}  {name_display:<{name_width}}  {member_count:>5}  {steps_str:>5}  {type_str:<6}  {desc_truncated}{focused}")
   490→    print()
   491→
   492→
   493→def _cmd_cluster_list(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   494→    plan = load_plan()
   495→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   496→    active = plan.get("active_cluster")
   497→    verbose: bool = getattr(args, "verbose", False)
   498→
   499→    if not clusters:
   500→        print("  No clusters defined.")
   501→        return
   502→
   503→    queue_order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   504→    sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache = _sorted_clusters_by_queue_pos(clusters, queue_order)
   505→
   506→    if verbose:
   507→        _print_cluster_list_verbose(sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache, active)
   508→        return
   509→
   510→    print(colorize("  Clusters (ordered by queue position):", "bold"))
   511→    for name, cluster in sorted_clusters:
   512→        min_p = min_pos_cache[name]
   513→        pos_str = f"#{min_p}" if min_p < 999_999 else "—"
   514→        member_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   515→        desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
   516→        marker = " (focused)" if name == active else ""
   517→        desc_str = f" — {desc}" if desc else ""
   518→        auto_tag = " [auto]" if cluster.get("auto") else ""
   519→        print(f"    {pos_str:>5}  {name}: {member_count} items{auto_tag}{desc_str}{marker}")
   520→
   521→
   522→def _cmd_cluster_update(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   523→    """Update cluster description and/or action_steps."""
   524→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   525→    description: str | None = getattr(args, "description", None)
   526→    steps: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "steps", None)
   527→
   528→    if description is None and steps is None:
   529→        print(colorize("  Nothing to update. Use --description and/or --steps.", "yellow"))
   530→        return
   531→
   532→    plan = load_plan()
   533→    cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(cluster_name)
   534→    if cluster is None:
   535→        print(colorize(f"  Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   536→        return
   537→
   538→    if description is not None:
   539→        cluster["description"] = description
   540→    if steps is not None:
   541→        cluster["action_steps"] = list(steps)
   542→        print(colorize(f"  Stored {len(steps)} action step(s):", "dim"))
   543→        for i, step in enumerate(steps, 1):
   544→            clean = _LEADING_NUM_RE.sub('', step)
   545→            print(colorize(f"    {i}. {clean}", "dim"))
   546→        if len(steps) == 0:
   547→            print(colorize("  Warning: 0 steps stored. Did you forget the --steps values?", "yellow"))
   548→        elif len(steps) == 1 and len(steps[0]) > 100:
   549→            print(colorize("  Warning: only 1 step stored and it's quite long. Check shell quoting.", "yellow"))
   550→    cluster["user_modified"] = True
   551→    cluster["updated_at"] = utc_now()
   552→    append_log_entry(
   553→        plan, "cluster_update", cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   554→        detail={"description": description, "steps": steps},
   555→    )
   556→    save_plan(plan)
   557→    print(colorize(f"  Updated cluster: {cluster_name}", "green"))
   558→
   559→
   560→def _cmd_cluster_merge(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   561→    """Merge source cluster into target cluster."""
   562→    source: str = getattr(args, "source", "")
   563→    target: str = getattr(args, "target", "")
   564→
   565→    plan = load_plan()
   566→    try:
   567→        added, source_ids = merge_clusters(plan, source, target)
   568→    except ValueError as ex:
   569→        print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   570→        return
   571→
   572→    append_log_entry(
   573→        plan, "cluster_merge", issue_ids=source_ids,
   574→        cluster_name=target, actor="user",
   575→        detail={"source": source, "added": added},
   576→    )
   577→    save_plan(plan)
   578→    print(colorize(
   579→        f"  Merged cluster {source!r} into {target!r}: "
   580→        f"{added} issue(s) added, {len(source_ids)} total moved. Source deleted.",
   581→        "green",
   582→    ))
   583→
   584→
   585→def cmd_cluster_dispatch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   586→    """Route cluster subcommands."""
   587→    cluster_action = getattr(args, "cluster_action", None)
   588→    dispatch = {
   589→        "create": _cmd_cluster_create,
   590→        "add": _cmd_cluster_add,
   591→        "remove": _cmd_cluster_remove,
   592→        "delete": _cmd_cluster_delete,
   593→        "reorder": _cmd_cluster_reorder,
   594→        "show": _cmd_cluster_show,
   595→        "list": _cmd_cluster_list,
   596→        "update": _cmd_cluster_update,
   597→        "merge": _cmd_cluster_merge,
   598→    }
   599→    handler = dispatch.get(cluster_action)
   600→    if handler is None:
   601→        _cmd_cluster_list(args)
   602→        return
   603→    handler(args)
   604→
   605→
   606→__all__ = ["cmd_cluster_dispatch"]
   607→
```

```
    29→def _print_queue_header(

   132→def _build_rows(display_items: list[dict], new_ids: set[str] | None = None) -> list[list[str]]:
   133→    rows: list[list[str]] = []
   134→    _new = new_ids or set()

   142→            conf_str = "—"
   143→            detector = "planning"
   144→            summary = f"[TRIAGE] {item.get('summary', '')}{blocked_tag}"
   145→            cluster_name = ""

   147→            conf_str = "—"

   149→            summary = item.get("summary", "")
   150→            cluster_name = ""
   151→        elif kind == "cluster":

   153→            continue
   154→        else:
   155→            conf_str = item.get("confidence", "medium")

   159→            cluster_name = plan_cluster.get("name", "") if isinstance(plan_cluster, dict) else ""
   160→
   161→        prefix = "* " if item.get("id") in _new else ""

   168→def cmd_plan_queue(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   169→    """Render a compact table of all upcoming queue items."""
   170→    runtime = command_runtime(args)
   171→    state = runtime.state
   172→    if not require_completed_scan(state):
   173→        return
   174→
   175→    top = getattr(args, "top", 30)
   176→    cluster_filter = getattr(args, "cluster", None)
   177→    include_skipped = bool(getattr(args, "include_skipped", False))
   178→
   179→    plan = load_plan()
   180→    print_triage_guardrail_info(plan=plan, state=state)
   181→
   182→    effective_cluster = cluster_filter
   183→    if not cluster_filter:
   184→        active_cluster = plan.get("active_cluster")
   185→        if active_cluster:
   186→            effective_cluster = active_cluster
   187→
   188→    queue = build_work_queue(
   189→        state,
   190→        options=QueueBuildOptions(
   191→            count=None,
   192→            status="open",
   193→            include_subjective=True,
   194→            plan=plan,
   195→            include_skipped=include_skipped,
   196→            cluster=effective_cluster,
   197→        ),
   198→    )
   199→    items = queue.get("items", [])
   200→    # Collapse auto-clusters into display meta-items
   201→    if plan and not effective_cluster and not plan.get("active_cluster"):
   202→        items = collapse_clusters(items, plan)
   203→
   204→    sort_by = getattr(args, "sort", "priority")
   205→    all_new_ids: set[str] = queue.get("new_ids", set())
   206→    # Merge review-based new issue IDs (since last triage)
   207→    review_new_ids = compute_new_issue_ids(plan, state)
   208→    all_new_ids = all_new_ids | review_new_ids
   209→    item_ids = {it.get("id") for it in items}
   210→    new_ids = all_new_ids & item_ids
   211→
   212→    if sort_by == "recent":
   213→        items = sorted(items, key=lambda it: it.get("first_seen", ""), reverse=True)
   214→
   215→    _print_queue_header(
   216→        items=items,
   217→        include_skipped=include_skipped,
   218→        plan=plan,
   219→        new_count=len(new_ids),
   220→    )
   221→
   222→    if not items:
   223→        print(colorize("\n  Queue is empty.", "green"))
   224→        return
   225→
   226→    # Determine which items to show
   227→    display_items = _queue_display_items(items, top=top)
   228→
   229→    # Render cluster banners first, then remaining items in the table
   230→    print()
   231→    for idx, item in enumerate(display_items, 1):
   232→        if item.get("kind") == "cluster":
   233→            _render_cluster_banner(item, idx, new_ids)
   234→
   235→    rows = _build_rows(display_items, new_ids=new_ids)
   236→    if rows:

   238→        widths = [4, 4, 12, 50, 16]
   239→        print_table(headers, rows, widths=widths)

   241→    if top > 0 and len(items) > top:

   243→        print(colorize(

   245→        ))
```

```
    12→def _rename_key(d: dict, old: str, new: str) -> bool:
    13→    if old not in d:
    14→        return False
    15→    d.setdefault(new, d.pop(old))
    16→    return True

    19→def _ensure_container(
    20→    plan: dict[str, Any],
    21→    key: str,
    22→    expected_type: type[list] | type[dict],
    23→    default_factory,
    24→) -> None:
    25→    if not isinstance(plan.get(key), expected_type):
    26→        plan[key] = default_factory()
    27→
    28→
    29→def ensure_container_types(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    30→    for key, expected_type, default_factory in (
    31→        ("queue_order", list, list),
    32→        ("deferred", list, list),
    33→        ("skipped", dict, dict),
    34→        ("overrides", dict, dict),
    35→        ("clusters", dict, dict),
    36→        ("superseded", dict, dict),
    37→        ("promoted_ids", list, list),
    38→        ("plan_start_scores", dict, dict),
    39→        ("execution_log", list, list),
    40→        ("epic_triage_meta", dict, dict),
    41→    ):
    42→        _ensure_container(plan, key, expected_type, default_factory)
    43→    _rename_key(plan["epic_triage_meta"], "finding_snapshot_hash", "issue_snapshot_hash")
    44→    _ensure_container(plan, "commit_log", list, list)
    45→    _rename_key(plan, "uncommitted_findings", "uncommitted_issues")
    46→    _ensure_container(plan, "uncommitted_issues", list, list)
    47→    if "commit_tracking_branch" not in plan:
    48→        plan["commit_tracking_branch"] = None

    51→def migrate_deferred_to_skipped(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    52→    deferred: list[str] = plan["deferred"]
    53→    skipped: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = plan["skipped"]
    54→    if not deferred:
    55→        return
    56→
    57→    now = utc_now()
    58→    for issue_id in list(deferred):
    59→        if issue_id in skipped:
    60→            continue
    61→        skipped[issue_id] = {
    62→            "issue_id": issue_id,
    63→            "kind": "temporary",
    64→            "reason": None,
    65→            "note": None,
    66→            "attestation": None,
    67→            "created_at": now,
    68→            "review_after": None,
    69→            "skipped_at_scan": 0,
    70→        }
    71→    deferred.clear()
    72→

    74→def normalize_cluster_defaults(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    75→    for cluster in plan["clusters"].values():
    76→        if not isinstance(cluster, dict):
    77→            continue
    78→        if not isinstance(cluster.get("issue_ids"), list):
    79→            cluster["issue_ids"] = []
    80→        cluster.setdefault("auto", False)
    81→        cluster.setdefault("cluster_key", "")
    82→        cluster.setdefault("action", None)
    83→        cluster.setdefault("user_modified", False)

    86→def migrate_epics_to_clusters(plan: dict[str, Any]) -> None:

    88→    epics = plan.pop("epics", None)

    96→        if name in clusters:

    98→        clusters[name] = {
    99→            "name": name,

   102→            "auto": True,
   103→            "cluster_key": f"epic::{name}",
   104→            "action": f"desloppify plan focus {name}",
   105→            "user_modified": False,
   106→            "created_at": epic.get("created_at", now),
   107→            "updated_at": epic.get("updated_at", now),
   108→            "thesis": epic.get("thesis", ""),
   109→            "direction": epic.get("direction", "simplify"),
   110→            "root_cause": epic.get("root_cause", ""),
   111→            "supersedes": epic.get("supersedes", []),

   113→            "agent_safe": epic.get("agent_safe", False),
   114→            "dependency_order": epic.get("dependency_order", 999),
   115→            "action_steps": epic.get("action_steps", []),
   116→            "source_clusters": epic.get("source_clusters", []),
   117→            "status": epic.get("status", "pending"),
   118→            "triage_version": epic.get("triage_version", epic.get("synthesis_version", 0)),
```
